```text
## Design

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Decision | Add a **Layering** switch to the collaborator dropdown. While it's off, nothing changes: the rows look the same as #116/#81 and the canvas uses the shared drawing order. Turning it on shows an up arrow, a drag handle, and a down arrow (**↑ · ↓**) on each row; the row order becomes the layer order (top row drawn on top). Each row can be moved one place with the arrows or dragged by the handle to any position. Turning the switch off hides the controls and returns the canvas to the shared order. |
| Alternates Considered | 1. A Front / Normal / Back control on every row (three fixed layers). 2. The ↑ · ↓ controls always visible on every row, with no switch, plus a "Reset order" button. 3. A separate "Layer order" panel or dropdown section that lists collaborators only for ordering, leaving #116's rows unchanged. |
| Rationale | The switch keeps the dropdown as simple as it is today for users who never need layering, and makes it obvious when the canvas is *not* in the shared order. The ↑ · ↓ controls sit next to the existing names, so users order the same rows they already use for visibility and locking. Alternative 1 can't put one collaborator above another when both are "Front", so it can't express a real order. Alternative 2 adds three controls to every row for everyone and makes it easy to change the order by accident, with no clear "off" state. Alternative 3 splits one collaborator's settings across two places and duplicates the list. |
| Consequences | While layering is on, the rows must be shown as a single list in layer order, so #116's section headers (In the room / Previously seen / Miscellaneous) become small per-row labels. Drag-and-drop needs keyboard- and touch-friendly fallbacks; the arrow buttons cover both. Turning the switch off keeps the chosen order, so turning it back on restores it until the page reloads. |
--
```

```text
Closes #80 (Sub-issue)

## What changed

Implemented local client-side visibility controls for collaborators' drawings, ensuring users can independently show or hide individual, all, or none of their peers' drawings without affecting shared scene data, sync status, or other clients' views.

### Ownership & Identity (`excalidraw-app`)
- Implemented a one-time `customData.creatorId` stamp applied by the client that first introduces an element to the room (ensuring edits never transfer ownership, and pastes or duplicates belong to the paster).
- Added a robust per-tab client ID system utilizing a `localStorage` pool, Web Locks, and `sessionStorage` to allow reopened tabs to correctly reclaim their ID.
- Introduced non-volatile `USER_IDENTITY` messaging on join, new-user creation, and renames, with optional `clientId` support added to pointer and idle payloads while maintaining compatibility with older clients.
- Implemented a locally persisted, per-room "previously seen" collaborator directory.

### Editor & UI Architecture (`packages`)
- Extended `AppState` with `hiddenCollaboratorIds`, `collaboratorDirectory`, and `viewModeBeforeSelfHide` (configured to never be persisted, exported, or synced).
- Established a single centralized visibility rule (`element/ownership.ts`) consumed across rendering, hit-testing, selection/binding chokepoints, the eraser tool, search, and exports.
- Configured hidden elements so they cannot be selected, erased, bound to, or exported (while preserving existing bindings), routing never-seen creators and untagged elements into a shared miscellaneous bucket.
- Added toggle, show-all, and hide-all actions, including automatically locking view mode with an explanatory banner when a user hides their own drawings.
- Created the collaborator visibility dropdown menu positioned next to the avatars for both desktop and mobile views.

## Why

Collaborative sessions can quickly become visually cluttered, making it difficult for users to focus on specific work streams or review individual contributions. Providing client-side visibility controls allows users to filter what they see locally without disrupting the shared state, modifying real-time sync, or interfering with what other collaborators view on their own screens.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** Added an extra redundant guard at the selection and deletion chokepoints that explicitly validates collaborator visibility before applying destructive scene operations. While strictly redundant with the internal state checks in `element/ownership.ts`, this additional failsafe intentionally compromises pure architectural separation to guarantee that hidden peer elements can never be accidentally selected, mutated, or permanently erased during bulk operations. This can be removed in the future if internal safe-guards are considered enough, or until architectural design is modified in a way to properly encompass a failsafe pathway.

**Encountered:** None. Implementation of this was built from scratch. Because of this, no test cases existed and had to be made.

## Notes

- Added 129 comprehensive feature tests covering multi-client collaboration flows through the real Collab/Portal, complete with control cases and mutation checks.
- All existing tests pass, and typecheck, lint, and Prettier checks are clean.

## Review

PR requires review from teammate.

Closes #81 (Sub-issue of #14)

## Why

In a shared room it's easy to accidentally select, drag, or delete a teammate's drawing while working next to it. #116 let users *hide* collaborators, but hiding removes the drawing you may want to reference. This PR adds a **visible-only (locked)** mode so a collaborator's work stays on screen as a reference but can't be changed from your client, without affecting anyone else.

This is a **carryover of #80 via #116**: #80 asked for per-collaborator visibility _and_ interactivity controls. #116 delivered visibility (ownership via `customData.creatorId`, the central rule in `element/ownership.ts`, the dropdown). This PR delivers the interactivity half, built on the same structures, following the design decision posted on #81.

## What changed

Adds a local, per-collaborator **lock** to the collaborator dropdown. A locked collaborator's drawings stay visible on my screen, but I can't select, move, resize, rotate, delete, erase, or text-edit them. Everything is local to my client: nothing is synced, saved, or exported, and other collaborators notice nothing.

### The rule (one pure function)

- `isCollaboratorInteractive` in `packages/element/src/ownership.ts`: **hidden → never interactive** (no interactivity without visibility); **your own bucket → always interactive** (can't be locked); otherwise **locked → not interactive**.
- Pure lock-list helpers next to it: `addLockedCollaborators`, `toggleLockedCollaborator` (ignored while hidden or for yourself), `unlockVisibleCollaborators` (hidden collaborators stay locked).
- Element-level wrappers `isElementInteractive` / `excludeNonInteractiveElements` (bound text follows its container; never-seen creators and untagged elements follow the miscellaneous bucket, as in #116).

### State and actions

- `AppState.lockedCollaboratorIds` (default empty; `browser`/`export`/`server` all `false`, so it's never persisted, exported, or synced and resets on reload).
- New actions `toggleCollaboratorLock`, `lockAllCollaborators`, `unlockAllCollaborators`. All use `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` (no history, nothing to sync).
- #116's hide actions (per-collaborator toggle and "Hide all") now also lock whoever they hide, so a collaborator who is shown again stays locked until unlocked (Criteria C).

### Enforcement

Interaction chokepoints now ask the interactivity rule instead of the visibility-only check: hit testing (click select, double-click text edit, path-target pick), `selectGroupsForSelectedElements` (marquee, lasso, Select All, groups), the App selection safety net (also re-run when the lock list changes), and the eraser. Rendering, export, search, and **arrow binding** stay visibility-only: per the amended Criteria E, arrows may still bind to locked (visible) elements, never to hidden ones. The element's built-in `locked` property is not used (it syncs and would break Criteria F).

### UI

Each dropdown row (in the room, previously seen, and "Untagged & unknown") gets a lock toggle beside its visibility toggle: disabled and shown locked while the collaborator is hidden, disabled and shown unlocked on your own row. "Lock all" / "Unlock all" are enabled only when they'd change something (both disabled after "Hide all"). Same component on desktop and in the phone main menu. #116's row button is unchanged (same test id, `aria-pressed`, text), now wrapped next to the lock button.

### Intended behavior: things attached to my elements still follow them

The lock blocks direct changes to a locked collaborator's elements. Changes that come from my own elements are kept:

- **Frames:** dragging my frame moves everything inside it, including locked elements. I own the frame's location, not the positions inside it.
- **Bound arrows:** a locked collaborator's arrow bound to my shape still follows my shape (bindings are kept, as in #116).
- **Path targets:** dragging my path still moves the elements it targets, like a frame.
- **Deleting my frame:** locked children are released where they are (`frameId` cleared), not deleted.

### Commits

- `78523efe` state logic · `027e95ef` enforcement · `458e868f` UI · `09013e13` fix: bulk buttons disabled when they'd change nothing (found in manual testing) · `d7e29804` repair mis-encoded characters in test names · `27ab30e7` AI log

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- Tests look actions up by name (`h.app.actionManager.actions[name]`) so a missing action fails as a readable assertion; a renamed action is only caught at test time, not by the type checker.
- `getSelectionWithoutHiddenElements` (and its inner `isHidden`) keep #116's names but now also drop locked elements. Renaming would mean editing #116's tests.
- `excalidraw-app/tests/collabLock.test.tsx` duplicates ~60 lines of socket/encryption/Firebase mocks from `collabVisibility.test.tsx` (`vi.mock` is per file).
- The dropdown trigger's badge still only reflects _hidden_ collaborators, not locked ones: including locks would change #116's badge behavior, since Criteria C keeps collaborators locked after they're shown again.
- Known limitation: hyperlinks on locked elements can't be clicked (locked elements behave like empty canvas for hit testing). Attached elements following mine (frames, bound arrows, path targets) is intended; see "Intended behavior" above.

**Encountered:**

- `getLocallyVisibleElements` serves both export and the bindable-element list in `App.tsx`, mixing "visible" with "interactive". Harmless for this PR (binding is visibility-only by design).
- `packages/element/tests/frame.test.tsx` has 30 skipped tests from upstream commit `0f81c302` (#7194, 2023); unrelated, untouched.
- In jsdom the viewport is 0×0, so the eraser (which only considers on-screen elements) can only be tested on shapes at the origin.
- The repo's `yarn prettier <files>` script already includes `.`, so it formats the whole repo rather than the given files.
- Locally, `yarn test:code` crashes when `excalidraw-room/node_modules` is installed (two copies of `@typescript-eslint`), so locally it needs `--ignore-pattern excalidraw-room`; CI lint passes.

**Not tested automatically, and why:**

- **A real two-browser session over the network.** The collab tests drive the real `Collab`/`Portal` classes, but the socket, encryption, and Firebase are mocked. Manual: opened the same room in two browsers against the local `excalidraw-room` server, locked/hid the other user, and checked every AC (A–H) by hand.
- **Visual appearance** (lock icon states, disabled styling, tooltips, dark mode, row layout). jsdom doesn't render CSS; checked manually.
- **Phone layout on a real device / touch gestures.** The phone test uses a mocked viewport and mouse events; checked manually with browser device emulation.
- **Lasso selection and the path-target pick** with locked elements. Lasso goes through the same `selectGroupsForSelectedElements` chokepoint that the marquee and Select All tests exercise; the path-target pick was routed through the rule but has no dedicated test.
- **Mutation testing** (StrykerJS) is run separately on the changed source files for D6.

**AI-written tests:** every test in this PR was written by Claude (Claude Code); the full list is below. Each test is named after the acceptance criterion it checks, and the expected values were written from the AC text in #81, not from the code's output; the "(control)" tests show each blocked action does work on an unlocked element, so a test can't pass just because nothing happens. How I checked the expected values: I manually tested functionality and compared it to each specific condition to prove it worked on the frontend. I checked each test case written by AI line-to-line and had it explain to me flow and coverage.
```

```text
Add User Priority and Layering
OPEN
# Issue Description

## Summary

Adds **per-collaborator layer ordering** to the collaborator dropdown from #116/#81. Each row gets an up arrow, a drag handle, and a down arrow (**↑ · ↓**). The order of the rows is the layer order on my screen: the collaborator at the **top** of the list is drawn above everyone else, the next one below them, and so on. I can drag a row by its handle to any position, or use the arrows to move it up or down one place.

Like visibility and locking, this is local to my client. It never changes the shared drawing order, the elements, or what other collaborators see.

## User Story

**As a** collaborator in a shared session, **I want** to put collaborators in the order their drawings are layered on my own screen, **so that** the work I care about isn't lost behind other people's drawings.

## User Scenario

A user is reviewing a teammate's diagram in a busy room, but other collaborators have drawn large shapes on top of it. They open the collaborator dropdown, grab the handle next to the teammate's name, and drag them to the top of the list. The teammate's diagram is now drawn above everyone else's on their screen, and clicking where the drawings overlap selects the teammate's element they can see. They press the down arrow on another collaborator to move them one place lower. Later they press **Reset order** and the original shared order returns. Nobody else in the room sees any change.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium

**Specific:** Greater Medium (8 points)

**Reason:** Builds on #116 and #81: ownership (`customData.creatorId`), the per-collaborator dropdown, and local-only AppState are already in place. This issue adds a local layer order and a single pure ordering function, and applies it everywhere drawing order matters: canvas rendering, hit-testing (so the element you click is the one you see on top), and export. It also adds a reorderable list to the dropdown, with drag-and-drop plus up/down arrow buttons. The drag-and-drop UI and the renderer/hit-test changes make this larger than #81, but it needs no new ownership, sync, or server work.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Criteria A: Layering switch and order controls.** The collaborator dropdown has a Layering switch, off by default. While it's on, each row (including my own row and the "unknown / miscellaneous" bucket) shows an up arrow, a drag handle, and a down arrow. The up arrow moves that collaborator one place up and the down arrow one place down; the top row's up arrow and the bottom row's down arrow are disabled. Dragging a row by its handle and dropping it moves that collaborator to the drop position. While it's off, these controls are hidden.
- [ ] **Criteria B: Layer ordering.** While the switch is off, the canvas looks exactly as it would without this feature. While it's on, every element from a higher collaborator in the list is drawn above every element from a lower one, and within a single collaborator elements keep the shared drawing order. Turning the switch off and on again keeps the chosen order until the page reloads.
- [ ] **Criteria C: What I click matches what I see.** Where elements overlap, clicking selects the element drawn on top in my local layering. If that element is locked (#81), the click passes through to the next interactive element underneath, as in #81 Criteria D.
- [ ] **Criteria D: Attached elements stay together.** A text label bound to a container is always drawn directly with its container, even if the label and container have different creators. Elements inside a frame are still clipped to that frame.
- [ ] **Criteria E: Shared-state integrity.** Reordering changes no element (`index` and `version` stay the same) and sends nothing new to other collaborators. Other collaborators see the shared order. My own "Bring forward / Send backward" actions still change the shared order as before, and on my screen they take effect within that collaborator's layer.
- [ ] **Criteria F: Local and non-persistent.** The layer order applies only to my client, isn't added to undo/redo history, and resets when the page reloads, matching visibility (#116) and locking (#81).
- [ ] **Criteria G: Works with visibility and locking.** A hidden collaborator keeps their place in the order and is drawn in that place when shown again. Locking or unlocking a collaborator doesn't change their place, and moving them doesn't change their lock or visibility.
- [ ] **Criteria H: New collaborators.** While layering is on, a collaborator who appears for the first time (joins the room or draws for the first time) is added to the bottom of the order.
- [ ] **Criteria I: Export follows my view.** PNG/SVG export uses my local layer order, the same way #116 exports reflect my local visibility.

## Resolved Questions

- **How are elements tied to collaborators?** Through `customData.creatorId` from #116; untagged and never-seen creators use the miscellaneous bucket.
- **Can I move my own row?** Yes. Unlike locking, layering my own drawings is useful (for example, moving my own sketches behind a teammate's).
- **What happens to z-order within one collaborator?** The shared drawing order is kept, so the existing z-order actions still work within each collaborator's layer (Criteria B, E).
- **How are #116's dropdown sections (In the room / Previously seen / Miscellaneous) handled?** The layer order is one list across all collaborators.
- **Do settings persist?** No. They reset on reload, like visibility and locking (Criteria F).

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

- Changing the shared drawing order (element `index`) for anyone.
- Per-element priority (layering individual elements rather than collaborators).
- Default order or default settings for new joining users beyond Criteria H (#83).
- Syncing or saving the layer order.
- Touch-specific drag gestures on phones (the up/down arrows work everywhere).

## Related

- **Depends on:** #116 (visibility, ownership, dropdown) and #81 (locking; interaction rules for Criteria C)
- **Design decisions:** see the Design comment below

## Head Issue

Issue (#14): Allow a togglable Layer in which all users are compartmentalized by interactivity and visibility.
```

```text
   190	export type CollaboratorVisibilityRow = {

   203	};

   205	export type CollaboratorVisibilityRows = {

   211	/**

   215	 * button applies.

   218	  inRoom,
   219	  previouslySeen,
   220	  miscellaneous,
   221	}: CollaboratorVisibilityRows): {

   223	  canUnlockAll: boolean;
   224	} => {

   226	    (row) => !row.isLockDisabled,
   227	  );
   228	  return {
   229	    canLockAll: changeable.some((row) => !row.isLocked),
   230	    canUnlockAll: changeable.some((row) => row.isLocked),
   231	  };
   232	};

   244	    "collaborators" | "collaboratorDirectory" | "hiddenCollaboratorIds"

   265	  }

   270	    extra?: Partial<CollaboratorVisibilityRow>,
   271	  ): CollaboratorVisibilityRow => ({

   273	    username,
   274	    isCurrentUser: false,
   275	    isHidden: appState.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has(id),
   276	    isLocked: !isCollaboratorInteractive(id, appState, selfId),

   295	            avatarUrl: collaborator.avatarUrl,
   296	          },
   297	        ),
   298	      );
   299	    }

   310	        Number(b.isCurrentUser) - Number(a.isCurrentUser) ||
   311	        (a.username ?? "").localeCompare(b.username ?? ""),
   312	    ),

   314	    miscellaneous: toRow(UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID, null),
```

```text
/**
 * How far the outer edge of an outside-mode clip must extend past the mask's
 * outline (in the mask's local coordinates) to cover all of `element`,
 * whatever the mask's rotation.
 */
export const getMaskOuterExtent = (
  mask: ExcalidrawMaskElement,
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
) => {
  const [x1, y1, x2, y2] = getElementBounds(element, elementsMap);
  const cx = mask.x + mask.width / 2;
  const cy = mask.y + mask.height / 2;
  const dx = Math.max(Math.abs(x1 - cx), Math.abs(x2 - cx));
  const dy = Math.max(Math.abs(y1 - cy), Math.abs(y2 - cy));
  return Math.hypot(dx, dy) + OUTER_EXTENT_PADDING;
};

/** the enabled masks that should clip `element` when rendering */
export const getActiveMaskElements = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
) => getMaskElements(element, elementsMap).filter(isMaskEnabled);

/**
 * whether the masked-out parts of `element` are previewed (drawn faintly, and
 * clickable): while one of its `masks` or the element itself is selected
 */
export const isMaskPreviewShown = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  masks: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
  selectedElementIds: Readonly<Record<string, true>>,
) =>
  !!selectedElementIds[element.id] ||
  masks.some((mask) => selectedElementIds[mask.id]);

/**
 * whether `element` can become (or keep taking elements as) a mask. Masked
 * elements can't be masks, so masks never chain.
 */
export const canBecomeMask = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
) =>
  isMaskType(element) &&
  !element.locked &&
  !isMaskedElement(element, elementsMap);

/** whether `element` can be clipped by `mask` */
export const canBeMasked = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  mask: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
) =>
  element.id !== mask.id &&
  !element.isDeleted &&
  !element.locked &&
  MASKABLE_TYPES.has(element.type) &&
  // bound text is clipped together with its container
  !(element.type === "text" && element.containerId) &&
  !isMaskedBy(element, mask.id) &&
  // masks never chain
  !isMaskElement(element, elementsMap) &&
  !isMaskedElement(mask, elementsMap);

type MaskOutline =
  | { type: "rect"; width: number; height: number; radius: number }
  | { type: "ellipse"; width: number; height: number }
  | { type: "polygon"; points: [number, number][] };

/** the mask's outline in its local (unrotated, top-left origin) coordinates */
export const getMaskOutline = (mask: ExcalidrawMaskElement): MaskOutline => {

/** opacity of the masked-out content previewed while the mask is selected */
export const MASK_PREVIEW_OPACITY = 0.2;

/**
 * Clips the context to the element's enabled masks (their intersection).
 * While one of the masks or the element is selected, the masked-out parts are
 * first drawn faintly so the user can see what the masks are hiding.
 */
export const applyMaskClip = (
  element: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: RenderableElementsMap,
  allElementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  rc: RoughCanvas,
  context: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  renderConfig: StaticCanvasRenderConfig,
  appState: StaticCanvasAppState,
) => {
  const masks = getActiveMaskElements(element, allElementsMap);
  if (!masks.length) {
    return;
  }

  if (
    !renderConfig.isExporting &&
    isMaskPreviewShown(element, masks, appState.selectedElementIds)
  ) {
    const boundTextElement = getBoundTextElement(element, elementsMap);
    for (const el of boundTextElement
      ? [element, boundTextElement]
      : [element]) {
      renderElement(
        el,
        elementsMap,
        allElementsMap,
        rc,
        context,
        renderConfig,
        appState,
        MASK_PREVIEW_OPACITY,
      );
    }
  }

  // successive clips intersect
  for (const mask of masks) {
    clipToMask(
      context,
      mask,
      appState.scrollX,
      appState.scrollY,
      getMaskOuterExtent(mask, element, allElementsMap),
    );
  }
};
```

```text
export const exportToCanvas = async (
  elements: readonly NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[],
  appState: AppState,
  files: BinaryFiles,
  {
    exportBackground,
    exportPadding = DEFAULT_EXPORT_PADDING,
    viewBackgroundColor,

  }: {
    exportBackground: boolean;
    exportPadding?: number;
    viewBackgroundColor: string;
    exportingFrame?: NonDeleted<ExcalidrawFrameLikeElement> | null;
  },
  createCanvas: (
    width: number,
    height: number,
  ) => { canvas: HTMLCanvasElement; scale: number } = (width, height) => {
    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    canvas.width = width * appState.exportScale;
    canvas.height = height * appState.exportScale;
    return { canvas, scale: appState.exportScale };
  },
  loadFonts: () => Promise<void> = async () => {
    await Fonts.loadElementsFonts(elements);
  },
) => {
  // load font faces before continuing, by default leverages browsers' [FontFace API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FontFace)
  await loadFonts();

  const frameRendering = getFrameRenderingConfig(
    exportingFrame ?? null,
    appState.frameRendering ?? null,
  );
  // for canvas export, don't clip if exporting a specific frame as it would
  // clip the corners of the content
  if (exportingFrame) {
    frameRendering.clip = false;
  }

  const elementsForRender = prepareElementsForRender({
    elements,
    exportingFrame,
    exportWithDarkMode: appState.exportWithDarkMode,
    frameRendering,
  });

  if (exportingFrame) {
    exportPadding = 0;
  }

  const [minX, minY, width, height] = getCanvasSize(
    exportingFrame ? [exportingFrame] : getRootElements(elementsForRender),
    exportPadding,
  );

  const { canvas, scale = 1 } = createCanvas(width, height);

  const defaultAppState = getDefaultAppState();

  const { imageCache } = await updateImageCache({
    imageCache: new Map(),
    fileIds: getInitializedImageElements(elementsForRender).map(
      (element) => element.fileId,
    ),
    files,
  });

  renderStaticScene({
    canvas,
    rc: rough.canvas(canvas),
    elementsMap: toBrandedType<RenderableElementsMap>(
      arrayToMap(elementsForRender),
    ),
    allElementsMap: toBrandedType<NonDeletedSceneElementsMap>(
      arrayToMap(syncInvalidIndices(elements)),

    visibleElements: elementsForRender,
    scale,
    appState: {
      ...appState,
      frameRendering,
      viewBackgroundColor: exportBackground ? viewBackgroundColor : null,
      scrollX: -minX + exportPadding,
      scrollY: -minY + exportPadding,
      zoom: defaultAppState.zoom,
      shouldCacheIgnoreZoom: false,
      theme: appState.exportWithDarkMode ? THEME.DARK : THEME.LIGHT,
    },
    renderConfig: {
      canvasBackgroundColor: viewBackgroundColor,

      isExporting: true,

      embedsValidationStatus: new Map(),
      elementsPendingErasure: new Set(),
      pendingFlowchartNodes: null,
      theme: appState.exportWithDarkMode ? THEME.DARK : THEME.LIGHT,
    },
  });

  return canvas;
};
```

```text
  arrow: NonDeleted<ExcalidrawArrowElement>,

  appState: AppState,

): { start: BindingStrategy; end: BindingStrategy } => {
  // binding chokepoint: arrows can't newly bind to elements of collaborators

    arrow,
    draggingPoints,
    screenPointerX,
    screenPointerY,
    elementsMap,
    bindableElements,
    appState,
    opts,
```

# Phase 1: Recon for #82 (no edits made)

The relevant suites all pass on this branch. I found one trap in export that would break AC E, and several spec questions that need your answer before Phase 2.

## Issue vs. prompt: one conflict

- **"Reset order".** The issue's User Scenario says "they press **Reset order** and the original shared order returns." No AC mentions a Reset button, and the Design comment rejected the alternative that had one (Alternative 2). In the chosen design, turning the switch off returns the shared order and keeps the chosen order. Your prompt matches the Design comment. I treat the scenario as out of date (see Q2).

## 1. Where the canvas gets its element list and order

- [App.tsx:2250-2266](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L2250-L2266): `render()` calls `renderer.getRenderableElements(...)` and passes `hiddenCollaboratorIds` and `collaboratorDirectory`. The result is saved as `this.visibleElements` ([App.tsx:2267](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L2267)).
- [Renderer.ts:177-228](packages/excalidraw/scene/Renderer.ts#L177-L228): `_getRenderableElements` is **memoized**. It takes `scene.getNonDeletedElements()` (the shared fractional-index order) at line 199, drops hidden elements at lines 115-122, then culls to the viewport at lines 210-219.
  - The memo key is the scene nonce plus the viewport and visibility props. The comment at [Renderer.ts:250-253](packages/excalidraw/scene/Renderer.ts#L250-L253) applies to us too: the scene nonce doesn't change when local state changes, so the layering fields must go into the memo key.
  - [Renderer.ts:260-277](packages/excalidraw/scene/Renderer.ts#L260-L277): while dragging into a highlighted frame, selected elements are temporarily re-sorted after the memo.
- [staticScene.ts:337-449](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L337-L449): draws `visibleElements` in array order. Embeddables and iframes are then drawn in a second pass on top ([staticScene.ts:451-535](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L451-L535)).
- **The grid depends on draw order.** [staticScene.ts:340-349](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L340-L349) draws a numeric `gridLayer` before the first element whose `element.index` is greater than it. That assumes the drawing order is the index order.

## 2. Hit-testing and other places that depend on draw order

- [App.tsx:6637-6705](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L6637-L6705), `getElementsAtPosition`: starts from `scene.getNonDeletedElements()`, then filters by #81 interactivity at line 6663, by hit, frame clip, and mask. Iframes go last.
- [App.tsx:6556-6613](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L6556-L6613), `getElementAtPosition`: picks the **last** hit element (or the one before it, if the top hit is only a bounding-box hit). Reordering the input list is enough for AC C. Locked elements are already filtered out first, so the #81 click-through comes for free.
- Other places that walk the list back to front:
  - [App.tsx:6764-6809](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L6764-L6809), `getTextBindableContainerAtPosition` (text tool, adding a label).
  - Arrow binding target: [binding.ts:622](packages/element/src/binding.ts#L622) leads to `getHoveredElementForBinding` ([collision.ts:400](packages/element/src/collision.ts#L400)). Also [focus.ts:243](packages/element/src/arrows/focus.ts#L243).
  - `getTopLayerFrameAtSceneCoords` ([App.tsx:7582](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L7582)) goes through `getElementsAtPosition`, so it's covered by the change above.
- **Embeddables are DOM overlays** ([App.tsx:1695](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L1695), [2635](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L2635)), so they always sit above the canvas.

## 3. PNG/SVG export

- [data/index.ts:49-70](packages/excalidraw/data/index.ts#L49-L70), `prepareElementsForExport`, applies local visibility. The image dialog, clipboard PNG/SVG, and resave all call it.
- **Trap:** [scene/export.ts:256](packages/excalidraw/scene/export.ts#L256). `exportToCanvas` calls `syncInvalidIndices(elements)`, which **mutates live elements' `index`** ([fractionalIndex.ts:213-225](packages/element/src/fractionalIndex.ts#L213-L225)) when the array order doesn't match their indices.
  - If a layered array reached it, the shared z-order would be rewritten, which breaks AC E.
  - SVG with "embed scene" also serializes `elements`.
  - Fix: apply the ordering only to the render list (`elementsForRender`) inside `exportToCanvas`/`exportToSvg`, never to the array passed in.
- `exportToSvg`'s `appState` parameter is a narrow type ([scene/export.ts:293-303](packages/excalidraw/scene/export.ts#L293-L303)). It needs the two new fields as optional, and `exportCanvas` must pass them.
- JSON, link, and Excalidraw+ exports ([actionExport.tsx:199](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionExport.tsx#L199), [LayerUI.tsx:196](packages/excalidraw/components/LayerUI.tsx#L196), [excalidraw-app/App.tsx:1026](excalidraw-app/App.tsx#L1026)) are not PNG/SVG, so AC I doesn't cover them. They keep the shared order.

## 4. How bound text and frame children are ordered and clipped today

- **Bound text is never drawn on its own.** It's skipped in the loop and drawn right after its container: canvas at [staticScene.ts:353-359](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L353-L359) and [421-432](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L421-L432), SVG at [staticSvgScene.ts:876-921](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L876-L921). [ownership.ts:25-34](packages/element/src/ownership.ts#L25-L34) already assigns a label to its container's creator. So sorting by bucket keeps labels with their containers (AC D).
- **Frame clipping is per element.** Each element whose `frameId` points to a frame gets its own clip ([staticScene.ts:364-381](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L364-L381)), and hit-testing has a matching rule ([App.tsx:6665-6680](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L6665-L6680)). Neither depends on order, so clipping holds after reordering.
- What does change: if a frame and its children have different creators, a child can be drawn above or below the frame's border. The clip is unaffected.
- Masks (`applyMaskClip`, [maskClip.ts:40](packages/excalidraw/renderer/maskClip.ts#L40)) also clip per element and don't depend on order.

## 5. The collaborator dropdown (`CollaboratorVisibilityMenu`)

- [CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx:313-354](packages/excalidraw/components/CollaboratorVisibility/CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx#L313-L354): a Radix popover around `MenuContent` (lines 154-307).
- The rows come from `getCollaboratorVisibilityRows` ([visibility.ts:240-316](packages/excalidraw/scene/visibility.ts#L240-L316)), which returns three groups:
  - `inRoom`: you first, then alphabetical.
  - `previouslySeen`: most recent first.
  - `miscellaneous`: the unknown bucket.
- These render as three `<section>`s at lines 247-304. Each `Row` is #116's visibility toggle plus #81's lock button (lines 56-94). A search filter appears at 8 or more people, and it hides the misc row while active.
- **Phone:** the main menu renders the **same** `CollaboratorVisibilityMenu` component ([MainMenu.tsx:61-74](packages/excalidraw/components/main-menu/MainMenu.tsx#L61-L74)). On desktop it's mounted in [LayerUI.tsx:401](packages/excalidraw/components/LayerUI.tsx#L401). So one UI change covers both.
- Actions live in [actionCollaboratorVisibility.ts](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCollaboratorVisibility.ts) and all use `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER`.
- AppState config is in [appState.ts:140-143](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L140-L143) and [289-292](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L289-L292); types in [types.ts:592-608](packages/excalidraw/types.ts#L592-L608).
- There is no drag-and-drop library in the repo.

## Implementation plan

**Phases 2-3: pure logic and state**

- In `ownership.ts`, a type `CreatorLayering = { collaboratorLayeringEnabled?: boolean; collaboratorLayerOrder?: readonly string[] }`, with the order stored top row first.
- `orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer(elements, state, elementsMap?)`:
  - Returns the **same array** when layering is off or the order is empty.
  - Otherwise does a stable sort by each element's bucket rank, using `getElementVisibilityBucket`, so bound text follows its container.
  - A bucket that isn't in the order yet goes to the bottom.
  - Covers AC B, D, G and H.
- Order-list helpers:
  - `moveCollaboratorLayer(order, id, toIndex)` and `moveCollaboratorLayerBy(order, id, ±1)` (no-op at the ends).
  - `appendNewLayerBuckets(order, buckets)` returns the same array when there's nothing new.
  - Never removes ids, so hidden or departed collaborators keep their place (AC A, G, H).
- AppState: `collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false` and `collaboratorLayerOrder: []`, both with `browser`/`export`/`server` set to `false` (AC F).
- Actions `toggleCollaboratorLayering` and `moveCollaboratorLayer`, both with `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` (AC E, F).
- In `componentDidUpdate`, while layering is on, add newcomers to the bottom of the order (AC H).

**Phase 4: wiring**

- Renderer: order before the memoized map and viewport cull, and add the layering fields to the memo key.
- `getElementsAtPosition`: use a cached ordered list keyed by scene nonce and order, because this is a hot path.
- `getTextBindableContainerAtPosition` and binding: see Q5.
- Export: order only the render list inside `exportToCanvas`/`exportToSvg`.
- These cover AC B, C, E and I. Bring forward / Send backward need no code change: they change shared indices, and the stable sort keeps their effect within the layer.

**Phase 5: UI**

- A switch row, then (while on) a single list built from a pure `getCollaboratorLayerRows` helper. Section headers become small per-row labels; the existing `ownRowHint`, `leftHint` and `miscellaneousHint` can be reused.
- ↑ and ↓ buttons (disabled at the ends).
- A handle using native HTML5 drag events, with the drag state kept in React rather than `dataTransfer`. That should make drag testable in jsdom with `fireEvent.dragStart/dragOver/drop`.

## Risks

- **Export index mutation** (above). There will be a dedicated test that `index` and `version` are unchanged after a layered PNG/SVG export.
- **Hit-test performance.** Sorting on every pointer move would be O(n log n), so the sorted list is cached.
- **Drag-and-drop inside the Radix popover.** A drag must not count as an outside click, and Firefox needs `setData` called for a drag to start. I'll check this by hand. Touch drag is out of scope per the issue; the arrows cover phones.
- **Single list plus the search filter.** If the list is filtered, ↑/↓ could mean "next visible row" or "next row in the full order", and dropping onto a filtered list is unclear. I propose that the arrows move within the full order and drag is disabled while a filter is active.
- **Single list and existing tests.** #116 and #81 tests find rows by test id, and while the switch is off nothing changes, so they should be unaffected.
- **Grid and embeddables.** See Q4 and Q6.

## Questions (blocking, per the "stop and ask" rule)

1. **Initial order the first time the switch is turned on.** The issue doesn't say. Options:

   - (a) The dropdown's current order: you, then in the room, then previously seen, then miscellaneous at the bottom.
   - (b) Derived from the shared order: the collaborator with the topmost element goes first.

   I recommend (a): it's predictable and the expected values come straight from what you see. Either way, the canvas changes as soon as the switch is turned on.

2. **"Reset order" in the scenario.** Can I treat the switch as the reset and add **no** Reset button? (Recommended.)
3. **AC H while the switch is off.** It only covers newcomers while layering is on. I propose that newcomers who appear while it's off also go to the bottom when it's turned back on.
4. **AC B can't be met for embeddables.** They are DOM iframes above the canvas, and upstream also puts them on top for hit-testing. I propose keeping that exception (layering applies among embeddables only) and noting it in the PR. Do you accept that?
5. **Arrow binding target and the text-container pick** are order-dependent "what's on top" checks that the ACs don't mention. I recommend routing both through the ordering function so they match what's drawn. Include them, or leave them on the shared order?
6. **Numeric grid layer** (a fork feature). With layering on, its position can look odd, because it assumes the drawing order is the index order. I propose leaving it unchanged and listing it as tech debt.

## Tech debt so far

**Encountered:**

- `exportToCanvas` mutates the `index` of the elements passed to it through `syncInvalidIndices` (upstream).
- The numeric `gridLayer` assumes the drawing order is the index order (staticScene).
- Embeddables are DOM overlays and can't be layered under canvas content.
- The renderer memo key must list every local-state field that affects ordering (from #116).
- `yarn prettier <files>` formats the whole repo (from #81).
- `docs/showcase2/README.md` is untracked on this branch. It isn't mine and I won't touch it.

**Introduced:** none yet. The planned collab test will copy the per-file socket mocks, as #81 did.

```text
export const getAllHoveredElementAtPoint = (
  point: Readonly<GlobalPoint>,
  elements: readonly Ordered<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>[],
  elementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  tolerance?: number,
): NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>[] => {
  const candidateElements: NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>[] = [];
  // We need to to hit testing from front (end of the array) to back (beginning of the array)
  // because array is ordered from lower z-index to highest and we want element z-index
  // with higher z-index
  for (let index = elements.length - 1; index >= 0; --index) {
    const element = elements[index];

    invariant(
      !element.isDeleted,
      "Elements in the function parameter for getAllElementsAtPositionForBinding() should not contain deleted elements",
    );

    if (
      isBindableElement(element, false) &&
      bindingBorderTest(element, point, elementsMap, tolerance)
    ) {
      candidateElements.push(element);

      if (
        hasBackground(element.type) &&
        !isTransparent(element.backgroundColor)
      ) {
        break;
      }
    }
  }

  return candidateElements;
};

export const getHoveredElementForBinding = (
  point: Readonly<GlobalPoint>,
  elements: readonly Ordered<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>[],
  elementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  tolerance?: number,
): NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement> | null => {
  const candidateElements = getAllHoveredElementAtPoint(
    point,
    elements,
    elementsMap,
    tolerance,
  );

  if (!candidateElements || candidateElements.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  if (candidateElements.length === 1) {
    return candidateElements[0];
  }

  // Prefer smaller shapes
  return candidateElements
    .sort(
      (a, b) => b.width ** 2 + b.height ** 2 - (a.width ** 2 + a.height ** 2),
    )
    .pop() as NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>;
};

export const getHoveredElementForFocusPoint = (
  point: GlobalPoint,
  arrow: ExcalidrawArrowElement,
  elements: readonly Ordered<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>[],
  elementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  tolerance?: number,
): NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement> | null => {
  const candidateElements: NonDeleted<ExcalidrawBindableElement>[] = [];
  // We need to to hit testing from front (end of the array) to back (beginning of the array)
  // because array is ordered from lower z-index to highest and we want element z-index
  // with higher z-index
  for (let index = elements.length - 1; index >= 0; --index) {
    const element = elements[index];

    invariant(
      !element.isDeleted,
      "Elements in the function parameter for getAllElementsAtPositionForBinding() should not contain deleted elements",
    );

    if (
      isBindableElement(element, false) &&
      bindingBorderTest(element, point, elementsMap, tolerance)
    ) {
      candidateElements.push(element);
    }
  }

  if (!candidateElements || candidateElements.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  if (candidateElements.length === 1) {
    return candidateElements[0];
  }

  const distanceFilteredCandidateElements = candidateElements
    // Resolve by distance
    .filter(
      (el) =>
        distanceToElement(el, elementsMap, point) <= getBindingGap(el, arrow) ||
        isPointInElement(point, el, elementsMap),
    );
```

Your answers settle most of the open points. Two of them raise follow-ups I need confirmed before Phase 2, and here is the binding answer you asked for.

## Q5: How binding works today

Binding currently ignores layering; it uses the shared order:

- `getAllHoveredElementAtPoint` ([collision.ts:324-358](packages/element/src/collision.ts#L324-L358)) walks the shared order from the top down. It collects every bindable shape under the arrow end, and **stops at the first shape with a solid fill**.
- `getHoveredElementForBinding` ([collision.ts:360-386](packages/element/src/collision.ts#L360-L386)) then picks the **smallest** of those shapes.
- #116 removes hidden collaborators' shapes first ([binding.ts:622](packages/element/src/binding.ts#L622), [focus.ts:243](packages/element/src/arrows/focus.ts#L243)). Locked shapes stay bindable, per #81's amended AC E.

If binding stays on the shared order, there's a visible mismatch with layering on. Suppose Bob's filled box is below Alice's in the shared order, but I've put Bob on top. When I draw an arrow onto the overlap, the scan reaches Alice's filled box first and stops. The arrow binds to Alice's box, which is drawn _under_ Bob's on my screen.

**Recommendation:** pass the elements through the layering function at those two existing chokepoints. That's one line each, using the `appState` already there, so the arrow binds to the top shape in my layering. The "smallest shape" rule is unchanged, and with layering off nothing changes. I'd do the same for the text-tool container pick ([App.tsx:6764](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L6764)).

## Export: reusing what's there

I won't add an export function. Both `exportToCanvas` and `exportToSvg` already call `prepareElementsForRender` ([scene/export.ts:150](packages/excalidraw/scene/export.ts#L150)). I'll give it the appState it needs and apply the ordering there, so one existing function covers PNG and SVG. It also runs after the `syncInvalidIndices` call and outside the embedded-scene JSON, so shared indices can't be rewritten. `prepareElementsForExport` stays visibility-only. Putting the ordering there would feed a reordered array into `syncInvalidIndices`.

## Follow-ups to A1 and A2

**Join order needs its own record.** There's no join timestamp today:

- `CollaboratorDirectoryEntry` has only `lastSeen` ([types.ts:98-102](packages/excalidraw/types.ts#L98-L102)).
- `collaborators` is rebuilt as a new `Map` on every update ([Collab.tsx:973-983](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L973-L983)), and a rejoin moves the person to the end.

So I'd store two local AppState fields. Both have `browser`, `export` and `server` set to `false`, so they reset on reload.

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `collaboratorJoinOrder` | Append-only. Records each collaborator the first time this client sees them, **whether layering is on or off**. This gives the "time" order. |
| `collaboratorLayerOrder` | `null` until you move someone. Turning the switch off and on keeps it (A1). |

- One pure function in `ownership.ts` computes the **effective order**:
  - `collaboratorLayerOrder` if it's set, otherwise the default: you on top, then `collaboratorJoinOrder`.
  - Anyone not yet in the list goes to the bottom, in join order (AC H).
  - The rows, the canvas, hit-testing, binding and export all use it.
- **Reset order** (A2) sets `collaboratorLayerOrder` back to `null`, which gives join order with you on top again.

Please confirm these four points:

1. **"Current user on top always"** applies to the default and to Reset only. You can still move your own row afterwards, per the issue's resolved question. Is that right?
2. **Reset button:** a **Reset order** button shown only while the switch is on, and disabled when the order is already the default. The issue scenario mentions it but the ACs don't, so I'll log it as your decision.
3. **Where previously seen collaborators and the miscellaneous bucket go.**
   - Previously seen: when I join a room, its "previously seen" list loads before live peers arrive. So they'd go first in join order (oldest `lastSeen` first), then live peers in the order they appear.
   - Miscellaneous: I propose it always starts at the bottom.
4. **Binding:** use the layered order as recommended above?

## Decisions log

- Initial order derived from the dropdown sections or from the shared order → **join order, current user on top**, stored so turning the switch off and on keeps it → layering should start from a familiar, time-based order and keep the user's changes.
- No Reset button; the switch acts as the reset → **Reset order button kept**, restoring join order with the current user on top → it matches the issue scenario and gives a way back without losing the switch state.
- AC H while the switch is off → **covered by the join-order record** → no separate rule needed.
- Embeddables can't be layered (DOM overlays) → **accepted: skip embeddables** → technical limit, noted in the PR.
- Numeric grid layer with layering on → **leave it, log as tech debt** → simple fix later.
- Export → **no new function; reuse `prepareElementsForRender` and update its checks** → avoid redundant export code.

## Tech debt

- Introduced (planned): two AppState fields instead of one, because Reset needs the join order kept separately from the custom order.
- Encountered: as in my previous message, plus the numeric grid layer issue, now confirmed as tech debt per Q6.

I'm waiting for your answers to the four points above and "Approved" before starting Phase 2.

```text
    72	) => {
    73	  const { [roomId]: _previous, ...otherRooms } = readRooms();

    75	  const currentRoom = {
    76	    updated: Date.now(),
    77	    entries: Object.fromEntries(

    79	        .sort(([, a], [, b]) => b.lastSeen - a.lastSeen)
    80	        .slice(0, MAX_ENTRIES_PER_ROOM),

    82	  };

    85	  // are pruned by recency

    88	    .slice(0, MAX_ROOMS - 1);

   103	/**
   104	 * Records that `clientId` was seen. Returns the updated directory, or `null`
   105	 * when nothing changed enough to be worth publishing/saving.
   106	 *
   107	 * @param username empty/missing = keep the known name (a client may not have
   108	 * picked one yet; that shouldn't erase what we know)
   109	 */
   110	export const recordCollaboratorSighting = (
   111	  directory: ReadonlyMap<string, CollaboratorDirectoryEntry>,
   112	  clientId: string,
   113	  username: string | null | undefined,
   114	  now = Date.now(),
   115	): CollaboratorDirectory | null => {
   116	  const prev = directory.get(clientId);
   117	  const nextUsername = username || prev?.username || null;
   118
   119	  if (
   120	    prev &&
   121	    prev.username === nextUsername &&
   122	    now - prev.lastSeen < SIGHTING_REFRESH_MS
   123	  ) {
   124	    return null;
   125	  }
   126
   127	  const next = new Map(directory);
   128	  next.set(clientId, { username: nextUsername, lastSeen: now });
   129	  return next;
   130	};
    return this.excalidrawAPI.getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted();
  };

  public getClientId = () => this.clientId;

  /**
   * Records a sighting of `clientId` in the current room's directory, saving
   * it when it changed. Returns whether it changed.
   */
  private recordSighting = (clientId: string, username?: string | null) => {
    if (!this.directoryRoomId) {
      return false;
    }
    const next = recordCollaboratorSighting(
      this.collaboratorDirectory,
      clientId,
      username,
    );
    if (!next) {
      return false;
    }
    this.collaboratorDirectory = next;
    saveCollaboratorDirectory(this.directoryRoomId, next);
    return true;
  };

  /**
   * (Re)publishes the directory to the editor. Also called after scene resets
   * (joining a room resets appState), so it's safe to call redundantly.
   */
  private publishCollaboratorDirectory = () => {
    this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
      appState: { collaboratorDirectory: this.collaboratorDirectory },
    });
  };

    document.addEventListener(EVENT.POINTER_MOVE, this.onPointerMove);
    document.addEventListener(EVENT.VISIBILITY_CHANGE, this.onVisibilityChange);
  };

  setCollaborators(sockets: SocketId[]) {
    const collaborators: InstanceType<typeof Collab>["collaborators"] =
      new Map();
    for (const socketId of sockets) {
      const isCurrentUser = socketId === this.portal.socket?.id;
      collaborators.set(
        socketId,
        Object.assign(
          {},
          this.collaborators.get(socketId),
          { isCurrentUser },
          // lets the editor tell which creator id is "you"
          isCurrentUser && this.clientId ? { id: this.clientId } : {},
        ),
      );
    }
    // collaborators who just left: refresh when we last saw them
    for (const [socketId, collaborator] of this.collaborators) {
      if (!collaborators.has(socketId) && collaborator.id) {
        this.recordSighting(collaborator.id, collaborator.username);
      }
    }
    this.collaborators = collaborators;
    this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
      collaborators,
      appState: { collaboratorDirectory: this.collaboratorDirectory },
    });
  }

  updateCollaborator = (socketId: SocketId, updates: Partial<Collaborator>) => {
    const collaborators = new Map(this.collaborators);
    const user: Mutable<Collaborator> = Object.assign(
      {},
      collaborators.get(socketId),
      updates,
      {
        isCurrentUser: socketId === this.portal.socket?.id,
      },
    );
    collaborators.set(socketId, user);
    this.collaborators = collaborators;

    if (user.id) {
      this.recordSighting(user.id, user.username);
    }

    this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
      collaborators,
      appState: { collaboratorDirectory: this.collaboratorDirectory },
    });
  };
```

Yes, you can reuse what #116 built: its collaborator directory already records join order, so the separate `collaboratorJoinOrder` field and any new tracking code are unnecessary.

## Join order comes from #116's directory

#116's `collaboratorDirectory` is in AppState as a `Map`, which keeps keys in insertion order. It is published by `Collab` from [collaboratorDirectory.ts](excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorDirectory.ts).

- **A new sighting is added at the end.** `recordCollaboratorSighting` copies the map and calls `set` ([collaboratorDirectory.ts:127-128](excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorDirectory.ts#L127-L128)). For an id already in the map, `set` keeps its position, so a rejoin doesn't move anyone.
- **It runs for every live collaborator** through `updateCollaborator` ([Collab.tsx:973-992](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L973-L992)), whether layering is on or off.
- So the directory's key order is the order this client first saw each collaborator.

**State shrinks to two fields.** Both are added next to `hiddenCollaboratorIds`/`lockedCollaboratorIds` in [appState.ts](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts), never persisted, exported or synced:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `collaboratorLayeringEnabled: boolean` | The switch (default `false`). |
| `collaboratorLayerOrder: readonly string[] \| null` | The stored order, `null` until layering is first turned on. Turning the switch off doesn't clear it, so off-then-on keeps it (AC B). |

**How each case works:**

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| First time on, or Reset | Fill the order with: you, then the directory keys in order, then any live collaborator not yet in the directory, then miscellaneous at the bottom. |
| Newcomer (AC H) | The pure ordering function puts anyone not in the stored list at the bottom, in directory order, below miscellaneous. |
| Your own row | Can be moved down after a reset. |

No `Collab.tsx` changes and no `componentDidUpdate` sync are needed.

**One catch on point 3.** On load, the directory is saved sorted newest-`lastSeen` first ([collaboratorDirectory.ts:78-79](excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorDirectory.ts#L78-L79)). So previously seen collaborators would come **most recent first**, not oldest first as you approved.

- **(a) Recommended:** accept most recent first. It matches #116's existing "Previously seen" section order and needs no change to #116 code.
- **(b)** Sort ascending in `loadCollaboratorDirectory`. That changes #116's file.

Which do you want?

## Binding (your point 4)

My description matches the code; I read it in [collision.ts:324-386](packages/element/src/collision.ts#L324-L386). One detail to add: the chokepoint at [binding.ts:622](packages/element/src/binding.ts#L622) filters the elements before the code splits into the simple binding path and the `COMPLEX_BINDINGS` one. One change there covers both paths. Focus-point re-targeting goes through [focus.ts:243](packages/element/src/arrows/focus.ts#L243).

## UI (point 2)

I'll reuse the existing [Switch.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/Switch.tsx), already used in `GridPanel` and `ImageExportDialog`. The layout follows #81's bulk-button rows:

```
[ Show all ] [ Hide all ]
[ Lock all ] [ Unlock all ]
[ Layering ⏻ ] [ Reset order ]   ← Reset grayed out while layering is off
  ── rows ──
```

Please confirm that "at the top above the names" means this row, directly above the rows and below the existing bulk buttons.

## Decisions log (updated)

- Initial order derived from the dropdown sections or from the shared order → **join order, you on top**, kept when the switch is turned off and on → a familiar starting order that keeps your changes.
- No Reset button → **a Reset order button** that returns to join order with you on top → matches the issue scenario.
- AC H while the switch is off → **covered by the join order** → no separate rule needed.
- Embeddables can't be layered → **accepted: skip embeddables** → they are drawn above the canvas.
- Numeric grid layer → **leave it, log as tech debt** → simple fix later.
- Export → **no new function; reuse `prepareElementsForRender`** → avoid redundant export code.
- Separate join-order field (`collaboratorJoinOrder`) → **reuse #116's directory instead** → use existing infrastructure.
- Your own row pinned on top → **on top only by default; you can move it after a reset** → matches the issue's resolved question.
- Reset disabled when the order is already the default → **Reset grayed out only while layering is off**, placed in a row with the switch → your layout choice.
- Previously seen and miscellaneous placement → **previously seen first, miscellaneous at the bottom** (oldest-first still open, see above).
- Binding stays on the shared order → **binding uses the layered order** at the existing chokepoints → the arrow binds to what's drawn on top.

## Tech debt

**Introduced (planned):**

- The default order depends on `collaboratorDirectory` keeping keys in insertion order. That is how `Map` works, but nothing in the code states it as a rule.

**Encountered:**

- `exportToCanvas` rewrites element indices through `syncInvalidIndices`.
- The numeric grid layer assumes drawing order matches index order.
- Embeddables are drawn above the canvas and can't be layered.
- The renderer's cache key must list every local setting that affects ordering.
- `yarn prettier <files>` formats the whole repo.
- The directory is saved sorted by `lastSeen`, so previously seen collaborators load newest first.

Please answer (a) or (b) and confirm where the switch row goes. I'll start Phase 2 when you type "Approved".

```typescript
/**
 * Issue #82 — unit tests for the pure layering logic in `ownership.ts`.

 * approved on it (Phase 1):
 *
 * - A: rows (incl. my own and the miscellaneous bucket) can be moved up/down
 *   one place or dragged to any position; the ends can't move further
 * - B: switch off → shared order untouched; on → a higher row's elements are
 *   drawn above every element of a lower row, shared order kept within a row;
 *   the order survives switching off and on
 * - D: a bound label is drawn directly with its container
 * - E: elements are never changed (index/version)
 * - G: hidden/locked collaborators keep their place
 * - H: a collaborator appearing for the first time goes to the bottom
 * - default order (decision on #82): me on top, then join order (#116's
 *   collaborator directory, in the order it was filled), miscellaneous last
 *
 * Arrays of elements are in drawing order: first = drawn first (bottom),
 * last = drawn last (top). Layer orders are top row first.
 */
import { arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { newElement, newTextElement } from "../newElement";

  CREATOR_ID_KEY,
  UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
  getCollaboratorLayerOrder,
  getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder,
  moveCollaboratorLayer,
  orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer,
} from "../ownership";

  newElement({
    type: "rectangle",
    id,
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    customData:
      creatorId === undefined ? undefined : { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId },
  });

const createLabel = (id: string, containerId: string, creatorId: string) =>
  newTextElement({

    text: "label",
    containerId,
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    customData: { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId },
  });

const ids = (elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[]) =>
  elements.map((element) => element.id);

/** directory as #116 fills it: insertion order = order first seen */
const directory = (...clientIds: string[]) =>
  new Map(clientIds.map((id) => [id, { username: id, lastSeen: 0 }]));

/** `collaborators` as the editor stores them; the first entry is me */
const room = (...clientIds: string[]) =>
  new Map(
    clientIds.map((id, i) => [`${id}-socket`, { id, isCurrentUser: i === 0 }]),
  );

/** me, alice and bob in the room; alice joined before bob */
const baseState = {
  collaborators: room("me", "alice", "bob"),
  collaboratorDirectory: directory("alice", "bob"),
};

const layered = (
  collaboratorLayerOrder: readonly string[] | null,
  extra: Record<string, unknown> = {},
) => ({
  ...baseState,
  collaboratorLayeringEnabled: true,
  collaboratorLayerOrder,

});

describe("orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer (the single ordering function)", () => {
```

# Phase 2 checkpoint: tests for the ordering logic (tests only)

## 1. Summary

I wrote 33 unit tests for the pure layering logic. They expect four new exports from `packages/element/src/ownership.ts`:

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer(elements, state, elementsMap?)` | The single ordering function that rendering, hit-testing, binding and export will share. It returns the **same array** when layering is off. |
| `getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder(state)` | You on top, then #116's directory in the order it was filled, then live collaborators not yet in the directory, then miscellaneous last. Used on the first switch-on and on Reset. |
| `getCollaboratorLayerOrder(state)` | The stored order, or the default if none is stored. Anyone not in the list yet goes to the bottom in join order (AC H). |
| `moveCollaboratorLayer(order, id, toIndex)` | One helper for ↑, ↓ and drag. Out-of-range or no-op moves return the same array, so the end rows can't move past the ends. |

Order lists are stored top row first. Element arrays are in drawing order: the first is drawn at the bottom, the last on top. Every expected value was worked out by hand from the AC text or from a decision you approved; none were copied from code output.

**Coverage by the checklist in your prompt:**

| Item | Test(s) |
| --- | --- |
| Switch off → original order | Same array returned. The control test shows the same setup **does** change the order when the switch is on. A further test covers having no layering state at all. |
| Higher collaborator drawn above lower | One test with three collaborators; one with interleaved elements. |
| Order kept within one collaborator | One test. |
| Bound text stays with its container | Label stamped by a different creator than its container. |
| Miscellaneous bucket and my own row can be ordered | One test each. |
| Hidden/locked collaborators keep their place | At element level, and in the order list (including a collaborator who left). |
| New collaborator goes to the bottom | Single newcomer, several newcomers in join order, and a creator outside a room. |
| Switch off and on keeps the order | Pure-level only: the stored order is used again. The action-level round trip comes with the actions (see point 4). |
| Extras | AC E: no element is changed and the input array isn't mutated. Default-order tests for the decisions you approved. Six `moveCollaboratorLayer` cases for the arrows, the end rows, and drag up/down. |

## 2. Files changed

- `packages/element/src/__tests__/ownershipLayer.test.ts` (new, uncommitted)

The untracked `docs/showcase2/README.md` isn't mine and I haven't touched it.

## 3. Test results

All 33 failures are `TypeError: (0 , <function>) is not a function`: 13 for `orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer`, 9 for `moveCollaboratorLayer`, 6 for `getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder` and 5 for `getCollaboratorLayerOrder`.

This is the right reason. The file loads, and the fixtures built at `describe` level with `newElement`/`newTextElement` work. Each test fails only when it calls a function that doesn't exist yet. Vitest leaves a missing export as `undefined`, so the failure shows up when the test calls it, not as an import error.

## 4. Things I'm unsure about

- **Where the actions and their tests go.** `toggleCollaboratorLayering`, `moveCollaboratorLayer` and `resetCollaboratorLayerOrder` need tests at the action level (AC G: "moving doesn't change lock or visibility"; AC F: no undo entry; the off-then-on round trip). Phase 3 asks only for "AppState fields and the minimum code to pass Phase 2". I plan to add the actions in Phase 4, alongside the collab and no-undo tests. Say so if you'd rather have them in Phase 3.
- **Where AC E is tested.** At this level I only check that the function doesn't change elements. The real checks (an export doesn't rewrite indices, nothing is sent to collaborators) are in Phase 4.
- **Your own row after a reload.** If your row isn't in the stored list (for example, it was saved before your id was known), it goes to the bottom like any newcomer, not to the top. That's consistent with AC H, but please confirm.

## Decisions log

- Initial order derived from the dropdown sections or from the shared order → **join order, you on top**, kept when the switch is turned off and on → a familiar starting order that keeps your changes.
- No Reset button → **a Reset order button** that returns to join order with you on top → matches the issue scenario.
- AC H while the switch is off → **covered by the join order** → no separate rule needed.
- Embeddables can't be layered → **accepted: skip embeddables** → they are drawn above the canvas.
- Numeric grid layer → **leave it, log as tech debt** → simple fix later.
- Export → **no new function; order inside the existing `prepareElementsForRender`** → avoid redundant export code.
- Separate join-order field (`collaboratorJoinOrder`) → **reuse #116's `collaboratorDirectory` insertion order** → use existing infrastructure.
- Your own row pinned on top → **on top only by default; you can move it after a reset** → matches the issue's resolved question.
- Reset also disabled when the order is already the default → **Reset grayed out only while layering is off**; [Layering switch][reset order] in one row directly above the rows, below the Show/Hide all and Lock/Unlock all buttons → your layout choice.
- Previously seen order: oldest first (a change to #116's loader) or newest first as stored → **newest first, as #116 already loads them**, accepted with "This all looks acceptable" → no change to #116 code.
- Binding stays on the shared order → **binding and the text-container pick use the layered order** at the existing chokepoints → the arrow binds to what's drawn on top.

## Tech debt

**Introduced (planned):**

- The default order depends on `collaboratorDirectory` keeping keys in insertion order. That is how `Map` works, but nothing in the code states it as a rule.

**Encountered:**

- `exportToCanvas` rewrites element indices through `syncInvalidIndices`.
- The numeric grid layer assumes drawing order matches index order.
- Embeddables are drawn above the canvas and can't be layered.
- The renderer's cache key must list every local setting that affects ordering.
- `yarn prettier <files>` formats the whole repo.
- The directory is saved sorted by `lastSeen`, so previously seen collaborators load newest first.

Waiting for "Approved" before Phase 3.
