```bash
cat >> packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorLayer.test.tsx <<'EOF'

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// UI (Criteria A, B, G and reset in the collaborator dropdown, desktop and
// phone)
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

describe("collaborator layering — dropdown UI", () => {
  const MISC = UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID;

  const openMenu = (scope: ParentNode = document) => {
    fireEvent.click(
      scope.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
        "[data-testid='collaborator-visibility-trigger']",
      )!,
    );
  };

  const getSwitch = () =>
    document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>(
      "input[name='collaborator-layering']",
    )!;

  const getResetButton = () =>
    document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(
      "[data-testid='collaborator-layer-reset']",
    )!;

  const queryControl = (kind: "up" | "handle" | "down", id: string) =>
    document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
      `[data-testid='collaborator-layer-${kind}-${id}']`,
    );

  const getUp = (id: string) => queryControl("up", id) as HTMLButtonElement;
  const getDown = (id: string) => queryControl("down", id) as HTMLButtonElement;

  const getRowElement = (id: string) =>
    document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
      `[data-testid='collaborator-row-${id}']`,
    )!;

  /** row ids in the order the single layered list shows them */
  const listedIds = () =>
    [
      ...document
        .querySelector("[data-testid='collaborator-layer-list']")!
        .querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[data-testid^='collaborator-row-']"),
    ].map((row) => row.dataset.testid!.replace("collaborator-row-", ""));

  const sectionTitles = () =>
    [
      ...document.querySelectorAll(
        ".CollaboratorVisibilityMenu__section-title",
      ),
    ].map((title) => title.textContent);

  /** a drag by `id`'s handle, dropped on `targetId`'s row */
  const dragRow = (id: string, targetId: string) => {
    const dataTransfer = {
      setData: () => {},
      setDragImage: () => {},
      effectAllowed: "",
    };
    const handle = queryControl("handle", id)!;
    const target = getRowElement(targetId);
    fireEvent.dragStart(handle, { dataTransfer });
    fireEvent.dragEnter(target, { dataTransfer });
    fireEvent.dragOver(target, { dataTransfer });
    fireEvent.drop(target, { dataTransfer });
    fireEvent.dragEnd(handle, { dataTransfer });
  };

  describe("desktop", () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      openMenu();
    });

    it("AC-A: the Layering switch is shown and off by default", () => {
      expect(getSwitch()).not.toBe(null);
      expect(getSwitch().checked).toBe(false);
    });

    it("AC-A: while the switch is off, no row shows ↑ · ↓ and #116's sections are unchanged", () => {
      for (const id of ["me", "alice", "bob", MISC]) {
        expect(queryControl("up", id)).toBe(null);
        expect(queryControl("handle", id)).toBe(null);
        expect(queryControl("down", id)).toBe(null);
      }
      expect(sectionTitles()).toEqual(["In the room", "Miscellaneous"]);
    });

    it("AC-A: (control) turning the switch on shows ↑ · ↓ on every row, including mine and miscellaneous", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      expect(getSwitch().checked).toBe(true);
      for (const id of ["me", "alice", "bob", MISC]) {
        expect(queryControl("up", id)).not.toBe(null);
        expect(queryControl("handle", id)).not.toBe(null);
        expect(queryControl("down", id)).not.toBe(null);
      }
    });

    it("AC-A: while on, rows are a single list in layer order, each labelled with its section", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      expect(sectionTitles()).toEqual([]);
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(DEFAULT_ORDER);
      expect(getRowElement("alice").textContent).toContain("In the room");
      expect(getRowElement(MISC).textContent).toContain("Miscellaneous");
    });

    it("AC-A: the top row's up arrow and the bottom row's down arrow are disabled", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      expect(getUp("me").disabled).toBe(true);
      expect(getDown("me").disabled).toBe(false);
      expect(getUp("alice").disabled).toBe(false);
      expect(getDown("alice").disabled).toBe(false);
      expect(getUp(MISC).disabled).toBe(false);
      expect(getDown(MISC).disabled).toBe(true);
    });

    it("AC-A: the down arrow moves a row one place down", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getDown("me"));
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(["alice", "me", "bob", MISC]);
      expect(layerOrder()).toEqual(["alice", "me", "bob", MISC]);
    });

    it("AC-A: the up arrow moves a row one place up", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getUp("bob"));
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(["me", "bob", "alice", MISC]);
    });

    it("AC-A: the new top/bottom rows' arrows become disabled after a move", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getUp("bob"));
      fireEvent.click(getUp("bob"));
      expect(getUp("bob").disabled).toBe(true);
      expect(getUp("me").disabled).toBe(false);
    });

    it("AC-A: an arrow moves the layer only, not the collaborator's visibility or lock", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getDown("alice"));
      expect(h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds.size).toBe(0);
      expect(h.state.lockedCollaboratorIds.size).toBe(0);
    });

    it("AC-A: dragging a row by its handle up to another row moves it there", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      dragRow("bob", "me");
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(["bob", "me", "alice", MISC]);
    });

    it("AC-A: dragging a row by its handle down to another row moves it there", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      dragRow("me", "bob");
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(["alice", "bob", "me", MISC]);
    });

    it("AC-A: dropping a row on itself changes nothing", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      dragRow("alice", "alice");
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(DEFAULT_ORDER);
    });

    it("AC-A: turning the switch off hides the controls and brings back #116's sections", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      expect(queryControl("up", "alice")).toBe(null);
      expect(sectionTitles()).toEqual(["In the room", "Miscellaneous"]);
    });

    it("AC-B: switching off and on again shows the chosen order", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getDown("me"));
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(["alice", "me", "bob", MISC]);
    });

    it("reset: Reset order is grayed out while the switch is off", () => {
      expect(getResetButton().disabled).toBe(true);
    });

    it("reset: (control) Reset order is enabled while the switch is on", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      expect(getResetButton().disabled).toBe(false);
    });

    it("reset: Reset order returns the rows to the default order", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      dragRow(MISC, "me");
      fireEvent.click(getDown("alice"));
      fireEvent.click(getResetButton());
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(DEFAULT_ORDER);
    });

    it("AC-G: hiding a collaborator from their row keeps their place in the list", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getUp("bob"));
      fireEvent.click(
        document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
          "[data-testid='collaborator-visibility-row-bob']",
        )!,
      );
      expect(h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has("bob")).toBe(true);
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(["me", "bob", "alice", MISC]);
    });
  });

  describe("phone layout", () => {
    beforeAll(() => {
      mockBoundingClientRect({ height: 400, width: 800 });
    });

    afterAll(() => {
      restoreOriginalGetBoundingClientRect();
    });

    it("AC-A: the Layering switch and ↑ · ↓ are in the main menu's collaborator section", async () => {
      act(() => {
        h.app.refreshEditorInterface();
      });
      expect(h.app.editorInterface.formFactor).toBe("phone");

      fireEvent.click(document.querySelector(".main-menu-trigger")!);
      const row = await waitFor(() => {
        const element = document.querySelector(".UserList-Wrapper__row");
        expect(element).not.toBe(null);
        return element!;
      });
      openMenu(row);

      expect(queryControl("up", "alice")).toBe(null);
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch());
      fireEvent.click(getDown("me"));
      expect(listedIds()).toEqual(["alice", "me", "bob", MISC]);
    });
  });
});
EOF
```

# Phase 5 checkpoint: the dropdown UI

## 1. Summary

The collaborator dropdown now has the Layering switch, Reset order, and ↑ · ↓ controls on each row, on desktop and in the phone menu. 19 new UI tests pass (60 in the editor test file), the full suite has no new failures, and it's committed as `bd1b1d7e` (not pushed).

**What you'll see:**

```
[ Show all ] [ Hide all ]
[ Lock all ] [ Unlock all ]
[ ⏻ Layering ] [ ↺ Reset order ]   ← Reset grayed out while Layering is off
 ↑
 ⋮  (avatar) Alice   IN THE ROOM   3  👁   🔓
 ↓
 ...
```

- **New switch row.** It sits directly above the rows, below Lock all / Unlock all, as you chose. It reuses the existing `Switch` component. Reset order is disabled only while the switch is off.
- **Switch off.** The dropdown is unchanged from #116/#81: same three sections, no extra controls. The tests check this directly.
- **Switch on:**
  - The rows become one list in layer order, top row drawn on top.
  - Each row keeps its #116 section as a small label ("IN THE ROOM", "PREVIOUSLY SEEN", "MISCELLANEOUS"), as the Design comment specifies.
  - The existing hints stay: "Hiding yours pauses editing", "Left the room", and the Miscellaneous hint.
- **↑ · ↓ controls.** They sit at the left of each row, including your own and Miscellaneous, and reuse existing icons: `BringForwardIcon`, `DotsIcon` (vertical dots, the handle) and `SendBackwardIcon`.
  - The top row's ↑ and the bottom row's ↓ are disabled.
  - Dragging the handle onto a row moves the dragged row to that row's position. A line shows the drop target.
  - The arrows are buttons, so they also work by keyboard and touch.
- **Name filter** (shown at 8 or more people). As in #116, Miscellaneous is hidden while filtering. The arrows still move past the next row in the full list, and dragging is turned off while a filter is active.
- **New pure helper.** `getCollaboratorLayerRows` in `scene/visibility.ts`, next to #116's row builder, puts the rows in layer order and tags each with its section.
- **Phone.** The phone main menu renders the same component, so it gets the same controls with no separate code.

## 2. Files changed (commit `bd1b1d7e`)

- `packages/excalidraw/components/CollaboratorVisibility/CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx`
- `packages/excalidraw/components/CollaboratorVisibility/CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.scss`
- `packages/excalidraw/scene/visibility.ts`: `getCollaboratorLayerRows`
- `packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json`: switch, reset, ↑/↓ and handle labels
- `packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: 19 UI tests added

No #116 or #81 test files changed.

## 3. Test results

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx` | **60 passed (60)** (41 from Phase 4, 19 new) |
| Full suite | **157 files passed, 1 failed; 2521 passed, 3 failed, 47 skipped, 1 todo**. The 3 failures are the same font snapshots that already fail on the untouched branch; I didn't touch them. |
| #116/#81 dropdown tests | all pass unchanged |
| `yarn test:typecheck`, `eslint --max-warnings=0`, `prettier --list-different` | clean on all changed files |

**The 19 UI tests:**

- **Desktop, switch:** off by default; while off, no ↑ · ↓ and #116's sections unchanged; (control) on shows ↑ · ↓ on every row including mine and Miscellaneous; while on, a single list in layer order with section labels; turning off hides the controls and brings the sections back; off then on shows the chosen order.
- **Desktop, arrows:** top ↑ and bottom ↓ disabled; ↓ moves a row down; ↑ moves a row up; the new top row's ↑ becomes disabled after a move; an arrow doesn't change visibility or lock.
- **Desktop, drag:** drag up; drag down; dropping on itself changes nothing.
- **Desktop, Reset:** grayed out while off; (control) enabled while on; returns the list to the default order.
- **Desktop, AC G:** hiding someone from their row keeps their place.
- **Phone:** the switch and ↑ · ↓ are in the main menu, and ↓ works there.

**Drag-and-drop in jsdom works.** The tests fire real `dragstart`, `dragenter`, `dragover`, `drop` and `dragend` events on the handle and the target row, with a stub `dataTransfer` object.

On the first run, the two drag tests failed because Testing Library made the stub's `effectAllowed` read-only, while real browsers let a `dragstart` handler set it. I removed that field from the stub; the component is unchanged. That failure also shows the drag tests really run the drop code.

**Coverage of the new UI code, and the gaps for the final pass:**

- **Previously seen rows while layering is on.** Nobody in the test session has left the room, so the "previously seen" branch of `getCollaboratorLayerRows` and its label are untested.
- **Name filter while layering is on** (hiding rows, drag disabled during a filter). The filter only appears with 8 or more people.
- **Defensive checks** for a missing `dataTransfer` or `setDragImage`.

The other "changed" lines in the report are #116's section markup, which only moved in indentation; #116's own tests cover it.

## Manual test steps (two browsers)

**Setup:**

1. Terminal 1: `cd excalidraw-room && yarn start:dev` (port 3002).
2. Terminal 2: `yarn start` at the repo root (app on http://localhost:3001; `.env.development` points it at `localhost:3002`).
3. Browser A, e.g. Chrome: open http://localhost:3001, click **Share → Start session**, set a name such as "Alice", and copy the room link.
4. Browser B, a different browser or a private window: open the link and set the name "Bob".
5. Draw three overlapping filled rectangles: A draws one, B draws one on top, then A draws another on top. Each should have a solid fill.

**AC A, B and Reset (in A):** 6. Open the ⋯ dropdown next to the avatars. Check: Layering is off, Reset order is grayed out, and there are no ↑ · ↓ controls; the dropdown looks as before. 7. Turn **Layering** on. Check:

- The list reads Alice (you) on top, then Bob, then "Untagged & unknown".
- Each row has ↑ · ↓ and a section label.
- The top ↑ and bottom ↓ are disabled.
- Reset order is enabled.
- On the canvas, both of Alice's rectangles are now above Bob's.

8. Press ↓ on Alice. Bob's rectangle is now drawn above both of Alice's, and Alice's two keep their relative order.
9. Drag Alice's handle (the dots) onto Bob's row. Alice is back on top. Also check that the drop line appears while dragging.
10. Turn Layering off. The canvas returns to the shared order (A, B, A), and the sections come back. Turn it on again: your chosen order is restored.
11. Move Alice down, then press **Reset order**. Alice is back on top.

**AC C:** 12. With Bob drawn on top of Alice in A's layering, click where they overlap. Bob's rectangle (the visible one) is selected. 13. Lock Bob with the lock icon and click the overlap again. The click goes through to Alice's rectangle. 14. Draw an arrow ending inside the overlap. It binds to the shape drawn on top.

**AC D:** 15. Add a label to one of Bob's rectangles by double-clicking it and typing. Move Bob down. The label stays drawn with its rectangle. 16. In B, draw a frame and draw an element in A that sticks out of the frame (inside it in B's frame). Reorder in A. The part outside the frame stays clipped.

**AC E (watch B the whole time):** 17. While A turns Layering on, moves rows, and resets, nothing changes in B: B keeps the shared order, and no edits arrive. 18. In A, select one of A's own rectangles and use **Bring forward** or **Send backward**. B sees the shared order change. In A, the rectangle moves only within Alice's layer.

**AC F:** 19. Reload A. Layering is off, and turning it on gives the default order (you on top). Ctrl+Z after reordering undoes nothing related to layering.

**AC G:** 20. With Layering on, move Bob to the top, hide Bob, then show Bob again. Bob is drawn on top again, and the row never moved. Locking or unlocking Bob doesn't move the row, and moving Bob doesn't change the eye or lock icons.

**AC H:** 21. With Layering on in A, open the room in a third window ("Carol"). Carol appears at the bottom of A's list, below Untagged & unknown. Carol's drawings are drawn under everyone in A.

**AC I:** 22. With a custom order in A, use **Export image** (PNG and SVG) and **Copy to clipboard as PNG/SVG**. The output matches A's canvas order.

**Phone:** 23. Use device emulation at phone width. Open the main menu (☰), then the ⋯ next to the avatars in the Collaborators section. The same switch, Reset, and ↑ · ↓ are there and work.

**Visual checks** (not automated): the switch's on/off states, disabled arrows, the drop line, the section labels, dark mode, and the row layout at phone width.

## 4. Things I'm unsure about

- **Drag inside the Radix popover in real browsers.** jsdom can't show whether a drag over the popover might close it or behave oddly in Firefox. I call `setData`, which Firefox requires for a drag to start, and use the whole row as the drag image. Please check steps 9 and 23.
- **The phone layout is getting crowded.** ↑ · ↓ add a narrow column to each row, so the name has a little less room (it's cut off with "…" when too long). Check at phone width.
- **Previously seen and name-filter cases** aren't tested yet (see the coverage gaps above). Step 21 covers previously seen indirectly: when Carol leaves, she should keep her place, labelled "PREVIOUSLY SEEN".
- **Where the controls sit.** I put ↑ · ↓ at the left of each row, the usual place for a drag handle. The Design comment says "on each row" without a position. Say if you'd rather have them at the right, next to the lock.

## Decisions log

- Initial order derived from the dropdown sections or from the shared order → **join order, you on top**, kept when the switch is turned off and on → a familiar starting order that keeps your changes.
- No Reset button → **a Reset order button** that returns to join order with you on top → matches the issue scenario.
- AC H while the switch is off → **covered by the join order** → no separate rule needed.
- Embeddables can't be layered → **accepted: skip embeddables** → they are drawn above the canvas.
- Numeric grid layer → **leave it, log as tech debt** → simple fix later.
- Export → **no new function; order inside the existing `prepareElementsForRender`** → avoid redundant export code.
- Separate join-order field (`collaboratorJoinOrder`) → **reuse #116's `collaboratorDirectory` insertion order** → use existing infrastructure.
- Your own row pinned on top → **on top only by default; you can move it after a reset** → matches the issue's resolved question.
- Reset also disabled when the order is already the default → **Reset grayed out only while layering is off**; [Layering switch][reset order] in one row directly above the rows → your layout choice.
- Previously seen order: oldest first or newest first as stored → **newest first, as #116 already loads them** → no change to #116 code.
- Binding stays on the shared order → **binding and the text-container pick use the layered order** → the arrow binds to what's drawn on top.
- Phase 2 tests → **approved; check coverage after every implementation step and go over the gaps together later** → hard to judge tests fully before the code exists.
- My proposal to add tests for the coverage gaps now → **add them after the Stryker run, for review** → review them together with the mutation results.
- Committing the regenerated SVG font snapshots → **leave tests and snapshots unchanged unless they relate directly to #82** → the font failures are most likely from the recent font feature.
- Your own row missing from a stored order → **old data belongs in Miscellaneous (or its own "Previously seen" row), as #116 already does** → no change needed.
- Where the actions go → **Phase 4, as planned**.
- Coverage-gap tests after Phase 4 → **write them once the UI and final implementation are done, in one final coverage pass** → cover the final coverage blocks together.

## Tech debt

**Introduced:**

- The default order depends on `collaboratorDirectory` keeping keys in insertion order. That is how `Map` works, but nothing in the code states it as a rule.
- `collabLayer.test.tsx` copies about 60 lines of socket, encryption and Firebase mocks from `collabLock.test.tsx`, because `vi.mock` applies per file.
- The ordering runs in two cached places (the renderer's cache and App's `getElementsInDrawingOrder`). Both use the same function, but each pays for its own sort when the scene changes.
- Tests run actions by name, as #81's do, so a renamed action is caught by the tests rather than the type checker.
- **New:** while layering is on, the dropdown renders its own list branch next to #116's sections branch, so the two share the `Row` component but not the list markup.
- **New:** drag-and-drop is native HTML5. Touch drag isn't supported, which the issue puts out of scope; the arrows cover touch.
- **New:** the `Switch` component has no test-id prop, so tests find it by its `name` (`input[name='collaborator-layering']`).

**Encountered:**

- `exportToCanvas` rewrites element indices through `syncInvalidIndices`.
- The numeric grid layer assumes drawing order matches index order.
- Embeddables are drawn above the canvas and can't be layered.
- The renderer's cache key must list every local setting that affects ordering.
- `yarn prettier <files>` formats the whole repo.
- The directory is saved sorted by `lastSeen`, so previously seen collaborators load newest first.
- `newElement`/`newTextElement` accept `id` at runtime, but their option types don't.
- 3 SVG font snapshots in `scene/__snapshots__/export.test.ts.snap` already fail on the untouched branch, likely from the recent font feature.
- Elbow-arrow routing (`elbowArrow.ts`) finds hovered elements through its own path, outside the binding chokepoints.
- **New:** in Testing Library, drag events get a `dataTransfer` whose fields are read-only, unlike real browsers, so drag tests need a minimal stub.

Waiting for "Approved", or for changes after your manual check, before Phase 6.

```markdown
Closes #82 (Sub-issue of #14)

## Why

In a busy room, one collaborator's drawing can end up buried under someone else's large shapes. The shared drawing order (`index`) belongs to everyone, so changing it to fix my view would change it for the whole room. #116 lets me hide collaborators and #81 lets me lock them, but neither changes what is drawn on top.

This PR adds **local layering**. I can put collaborators in the order their drawings are layered on _my_ screen, without touching the shared order or what anyone else sees. It follows the Design comment on #82: a **Layering** switch in the collaborator dropdown. While it's off, nothing changes. While it's on, each row gets **↑ · ↓** controls and the row order is the layer order (top row drawn on top).

It builds on #116 (ownership via `customData.creatorId`, the rules in `element/ownership.ts`, the dropdown, and the collaborator directory) and #81 (the interactivity rule, locking).

## What changed

### The rule (one pure function)

`orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer` in `packages/element/src/ownership.ts`:

- While layering is off, it returns the input array as is.
- While it's on, it does a stable sort by each element's layer rank. A higher row is drawn above every element of a lower row, and each collaborator keeps the shared order.
- Bound text follows its container: it reuses #116's `getElementVisibilityBucket`, so labels stay with their shapes and untagged or never-seen creators fall into the miscellaneous bucket.
- Buckets not in the order go below everyone.
- It never changes an element.

Pure helpers next to it:

- `getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder`: me on top, then everyone in **join order**, then miscellaneous last. Join order is the insertion order of #116's `collaboratorDirectory`, so no new tracking was needed.
- `getCollaboratorLayerOrder`: the stored order, with newcomers added to the bottom (AC H). Ids are never dropped, so collaborators who are hidden or have left keep their place (AC G).
- `moveCollaboratorLayer`: move to a position, clamped; used by the arrows and by drag.

### State and actions

- `AppState.collaboratorLayeringEnabled` (default `false`) and `AppState.collaboratorLayerOrder` (default `null`).
  - Both are set to `browser`/`export`/`server` `false`, like #81's `lockedCollaboratorIds`. They are never persisted, exported, or synced, and they reset on reload (AC F).
- New actions, all with `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` (no history, nothing to sync):
  - `toggleCollaboratorLayering`: the first switch-on stores the default order; switching off keeps it.
  - `moveCollaboratorLayer` and `resetCollaboratorLayerOrder`: both only work while layering is on.

### Every "what's on top" path uses the same function

So what's drawn, what's clicked, what an arrow binds to, and what's exported always agree.

- **Canvas** (`scene/Renderer.ts`): orders the elements before its memoized element map. The layer order is part of the memo key; the option is optional, so #116's callers are unchanged.
- **Hit-testing** (`App.tsx`): `getElementsAtPosition` and the text-container pick use `getElementsInDrawingOrder()`, which is cached per scene change and layer order. #81's click-through to the next interactive element still works.
  - `getLocalLayerOrder()` returns the same array while the order's contents don't change, so peers' cursor updates (which replace `collaborators`) don't invalidate the caches.
- **Arrow binding**: #116's `getBindableElements()` (all App binding call sites) and the `binding.ts`/`focus.ts` chokepoints use the drawing order, so an arrow binds to the shape on top on my screen.
- **PNG/SVG export** (AC I): ordered inside the existing `prepareElementsForRender`, with no new export function. It runs _after_ `exportToCanvas`'s `syncInvalidIndices` and outside the embedded-scene JSON, so the shared indices are never rewritten (AC E).
- The shared z-order actions (`zindex.ts`) are unchanged. My own Bring forward / Send backward still change the shared order and, on my screen, take effect within my layer (AC E).

### UI

In the collaborator dropdown, desktop and the phone main menu (same component):

- A **[Layering switch][reset order]** row below Lock all / Unlock all. It reuses `Switch`. Reset order is disabled while layering is off and returns to the default order (me on top).
- While layering is on:
  - The rows become a single list in layer order, and #116's section titles become small per-row labels.
  - Each row, including mine and "Untagged & unknown", gets ↑, a drag handle, and ↓. They reuse the z-order and dots icons.
  - The top row's ↑ and the bottom row's ↓ are disabled.
  - Dragging the handle onto a row moves the dragged row there, using native drag and drop. Dragging is off while filtering by name; the arrows still work.
- While layering is off, the dropdown renders exactly as in #116/#81.

### Commits

- `f1673050` ordering logic and state
- `0d1f6278` rendering, hit-testing, binding, export, actions
- `bd1b1d7e` UI
- `4e48135b` fix: the drag handle couldn't be dragged in browsers (found in manual testing; `all: unset` removed the browser's `[draggable]` styles)
- `379f9fab` AI log for the spec

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- The default order relies on `collaboratorDirectory` (a `Map`) keeping insertion order as the join order. `Map` guarantees this, but nothing in the code states it as a rule.
- The ordering runs in two cached places: the renderer's element map and App's `getElementsInDrawingOrder`. Both call the same function, so they can't disagree, but each sorts once per scene change.
- While layering is on, the dropdown renders its own list branch next to #116's sections branch. They share the `Row` component but not the list markup.
- `excalidraw-app/tests/collabLayer.test.tsx` duplicates about 60 lines of socket, encryption, and Firebase mocks from `collabLock.test.tsx`, because `vi.mock` applies per file (as in #81).
- Tests look actions up by name (`actionManager.actions[name]`), as #81's do, so a renamed action is caught at test time, not by the type checker.
- `Switch` has no test-id prop, so tests find the Layering switch by its `name`.
- Drag-and-drop is native HTML5, so touch drag isn't supported. The issue puts touch drag out of scope, and the ↑/↓ buttons work everywhere.

**Encountered:**

- `exportToCanvas` mutates the `index` of the elements it's given (`syncInvalidIndices`). Reordering the elements _passed into_ export would have rewritten shared indices. The ordering is applied only to the render list for that reason.
- A numeric `gridLayer` (fork feature) assumes drawing order matches index order (`staticScene.ts`), so with layering on the grid can land in an odd place. Left as is, to fix later.
- Embeddables are DOM overlays above the canvas, so they can't be layered under canvas content. Skipped by decision.
- The renderer's memo key must list every piece of local state that affects ordering (#116's note applies here too).
- Elbow-arrow routing (`elbowArrow.ts`) finds hovered elements through its own path, outside the binding chokepoints. It still uses the shared order.
- The directory is saved sorted by `lastSeen`, so previously seen collaborators load newest first. Kept as is, without changing #116 code.
- `newElement`/`newTextElement` accept `id` at runtime, but their option types don't.
- 3 SVG font snapshots in `packages/excalidraw/tests/scene/__snapshots__/export.test.ts.snap` (`exportToSvg` › default arguments / CJK font / exportEmbedScene) already fail on `master`, likely from the recent font work. Only `@font-face` data differs; left untouched.
- `yarn prettier <files>` formats the whole repo. Locally, lint needs `--ignore-pattern excalidraw-room`.
- Testing Library gives drag events a `dataTransfer` with read-only fields, unlike browsers, so drag tests use a minimal stub.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A** Layering switch and ↑ · ↓ controls (incl. my row and miscellaneous; end arrows disabled; drag to drop position; hidden while off) | `ownershipLayer.test.ts`: `moveCollaboratorLayer` (AC-A), the miscellaneous and own-row ordering cases. `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "switch and order", and "dropdown UI" desktop + phone | Unit, integration (editor), component (desktop + phone) | **AC**. **Other**: Reset order (shown in the issue's User Scenario, not in an AC) and the default order (me on top, then join order) are the author's decisions made during implementation |
| **B** Layer ordering (off = unchanged; higher above lower; shared order within a collaborator; off/on keeps the order) | `ownershipLayer.test.ts`: `orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer` AC-B cases, `getCollaboratorLayerOrder`. `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "Criteria B (drawing)" (what App actually draws), off/on in "switch and order" and "dropdown UI" | Unit, integration, component | **AC**. Each "nothing changes" test has a control showing the same setup does change with layering on |
| **C** What I click matches what I see (incl. #81 click-through) | `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "Criteria C" (control with switch off, top element selected, locked top passes through), arrow binding (control + on) | Integration (real pointer events) | **AC**; **upstream behavior** for #81's click-through (#81 AC D). **Other**: arrows binding to the shape on top is the author's decision |
| **D** Attached elements stay together (labels with containers; frame children still clipped) | `ownershipLayer.test.ts`: AC-D label case. `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "Criteria D" (label drawn right after its container; frame child keeps its frame, click inside selects it, clipped part outside selects nothing, plus a control showing layering does reorder frame and child) | Unit, integration | **AC** |
| **E** Shared-state integrity (no `index`/`version` change; nothing sent; others see the shared order; Bring forward / Send backward within my layer) | `collabLayer.test.tsx` (real Collab/Portal, recorded socket): nothing sent, no index/version change, a later edit sends the shared indices, peer updates still arrive with the scene in shared order, plus 2 controls. `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "Criteria E (editor side)", Bring forward within my layer, export changes no index/version. `ownershipLayer.test.ts`: AC-E (no element or input mutation) | Integration (app + collab), integration (editor), unit | **AC** |
| **F** Local and non-persistent (no undo; reset on reload) | `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "Criteria F" (no undo entries; not in local storage, export, or server state; reset on reload via `restoreAppState`) | Integration | **AC**; matches #116/#81 (**upstream behavior** of those features' tests) |
| **G** Works with visibility and locking | `ownershipLayer.test.ts`: AC-G cases. `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "Criteria G" (hiding/locking keeps the place, moving keeps hidden/locked, a re-shown collaborator is drawn in their place), dropdown AC-G case | Unit, integration, component | **AC** |
| **H** New collaborators added to the bottom | `ownershipLayer.test.ts`: AC-H cases (one or several newcomers in join order, unknown creator). `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "Criteria H" (joins while on → bottom of the list; drawn below everyone) | Unit, integration | **AC**. **Other**: "in join order" for several newcomers is the author's decision |
| **I** Export follows my view | `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: "Criteria I" (SVG through the real "copy as SVG" path, PNG draw order, each with a switch-off control) | Integration | **AC** |

**Not tested automatically, and why:**

- **A real two-browser session over the network.** The collab tests drive the real `Collab`/`Portal` classes, but the socket, encryption, and Firebase are mocked. Manual: two browsers against the local `excalidraw-room` server (room on 3002, app on 3001), checking each AC (A–I) by hand.
- **Visual appearance**: switch states, disabled arrows, the drop indicator, section labels, dark mode, and row layout at phone width. jsdom doesn't render CSS. Checked manually.
- **Native drag-and-drop in a real browser.** The component tests fire real drag events in jsdom, but jsdom applies no CSS, so they couldn't catch the `all: unset` bug fixed in `4e48135b`. It was reproduced and verified with real mouse input in Chromium (Edge, via `puppeteer-core`) and by hand.
- **Phone on a real device / touch.** Touch drag is out of scope per the issue. The phone test uses a mocked viewport; the arrows were checked manually with device emulation.
- **Paths routed through the ordering function but not reached by a test yet**:
```

# Phase 6 checkpoint: drag fix, full check, PR draft

## 1. Summary

The handle drag now works in a real browser. All checks pass apart from the 3 SVG font snapshots that also fail on master, and the PR description is drafted in `pr-82.md`.

**The drag fix (commit `4e48135b`).** I reproduced your bug in a real browser: a script drove headless Edge (via the already-installed `puppeteer-core`) against your running dev server, with real mouse input.

- **Symptom:** the mouse went down on the handle, but `dragstart` never fired.
- **Narrowing it down:**
  - A plain draggable `<div>` dragged fine, inside and outside the popover.
  - The same `<div>` stopped dragging once it got the handle's CSS class.
  - Trying the declarations one at a time pinned it to `all: unset`.
- **Cause:** browsers make `draggable="true"` work through a built-in CSS rule, and `all: unset` removes that rule as well. jsdom applies no CSS, so the component tests couldn't catch this.
- **Fix:** only the ↑/↓ buttons get `all: unset` now.
- **Also:** a row drop now stops at the list, so it never reaches the canvas's own drop handler. That handler ignored our row ids anyway, so nothing visible changed.
- **Verified in Edge:** dragging Bob up gives `[bob, me, alice, misc]`, dragging me down gives `[alice, bob, me, misc]`, the popover stays open, and no element is added to the canvas.

**Is master the right comparison?** `origin/master` (`46d92abb`) is exactly this branch's base; the only change before my commits is the spec's AI log. So nothing that passed on master fails now.

## Decisions log

- Initial order derived from the dropdown sections or from the shared order → **join order, you on top**, kept when the switch is turned off and on → a familiar starting order that keeps your changes.
- No Reset button → **a Reset order button** that returns to join order with you on top → matches the issue scenario.
- AC H while the switch is off → **covered by the join order** → no separate rule needed.
- Embeddables can't be layered → **accepted: skip embeddables** → they are drawn above the canvas.
- Numeric grid layer → **leave it, log as tech debt** → simple fix later.
- Export → **no new function; order inside the existing `prepareElementsForRender`** → avoid redundant export code.
- Separate join-order field (`collaboratorJoinOrder`) → **reuse #116's `collaboratorDirectory` insertion order** → use existing infrastructure.
- Your own row pinned on top → **on top only by default; you can move it after a reset** → matches the issue's resolved question.
- Reset also disabled when the order is already the default → **Reset grayed out only while layering is off**; [Layering switch][reset order] in one row directly above the rows → your layout choice.
- Previously seen order: oldest first or newest first as stored → **newest first, as #116 already loads them** → no change to #116 code.
- Binding stays on the shared order → **binding and the text-container pick use the layered order** → the arrow binds to what's drawn on top.
- Phase 2 tests → **approved; check coverage after every implementation step and go over the gaps together later** → hard to judge tests fully before the code exists.
- My proposal to add tests for the coverage gaps now → **add them after the Stryker run, for review** → review them together with the mutation results.
- Committing the regenerated SVG font snapshots → **leave tests and snapshots unchanged unless they relate directly to #82** → the font failures are most likely from the recent font feature.
- Your own row missing from a stored order → **old data belongs in Miscellaneous (or its own "Previously seen" row), as #116 already does** → no change needed.
- Where the actions go → **Phase 4, as planned**.
- Coverage-gap tests after Phase 4 → **write them once the UI and final implementation are done, in one final coverage pass** → cover the final coverage blocks together.
- Phase 5 passed the jsdom tests → **you found in manual testing that dragging by the handle didn't work; fix it before Phase 6** → root cause `all: unset` fixed in `4e48135b`; row drops also stop at the list.

## Tech debt

**Introduced:**

- The default order depends on `collaboratorDirectory` keeping keys in insertion order. That is how `Map` works, but nothing in the code states it as a rule.
- `collabLayer.test.tsx` copies about 60 lines of socket, encryption and Firebase mocks from `collabLock.test.tsx`, because `vi.mock` applies per file.
- The ordering runs in two cached places (the renderer's cache and App's `getElementsInDrawingOrder`). Both use the same function, but each pays for its own sort when the scene changes.
- Tests run actions by name, as #81's do, so a renamed action is caught by the tests rather than the type checker.
- While layering is on, the dropdown renders its own list branch next to #116's sections branch; they share the `Row` component but not the list markup.
- Drag-and-drop is native HTML5, so touch drag isn't supported (out of scope per the issue; the arrows cover touch).
- The `Switch` component has no test-id prop, so tests find it by its `name`.

**Encountered:**

- `exportToCanvas` rewrites element indices through `syncInvalidIndices`.
- The numeric grid layer assumes drawing order matches index order.
- Embeddables are drawn above the canvas and can't be layered.
- The renderer's cache key must list every local setting that affects ordering.
- `yarn prettier <files>` formats the whole repo, and local lint needs `--ignore-pattern excalidraw-room`.
- The directory is saved sorted by `lastSeen`, so previously seen collaborators load newest first.
- `newElement`/`newTextElement` accept `id` at runtime, but their option types don't.
- 3 SVG font snapshots in `scene/__snapshots__/export.test.ts.snap` fail on master, likely from the recent font feature.
- Elbow-arrow routing (`elbowArrow.ts`) finds hovered elements through its own path, outside the binding chokepoints.
- Testing Library gives drag events a `dataTransfer` with read-only fields, unlike real browsers.
- **New:** jsdom doesn't apply CSS, so CSS-driven behavior like dragging needs a real browser. `puppeteer-core` plus the installed Edge worked for this.

I haven't pushed, opened a PR, or merged anything. Next: you run Stryker, then I write the coverage-gap tests for your review. Waiting for your go-ahead.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-18 20:52:51Z)**_

Both drag bugs are fixed and committed as `e31b0315` (not pushed), and I checked both in a real browser (Edge, real mouse input).

## 1. The two bugs

**Drop line missing on the top row.**

- **Cause:** the line was drawn just _outside_ the target row's top edge. The list scrolls, and a scroll box clips anything above its first row.
- **Fix:** the line is now drawn _inside_ the row, so it can't be clipped. It also goes on the side where the row will land: the top edge when dragging up, the bottom edge when dragging down. Before, it was always on top, which was wrong for downward drags.
- **Verified:** mid-drag in Edge, the top row gets the line. A screenshot shows it on "Me (you)".

**"No drop" cursor flashing.**

- **Cause:** confirmed in Edge. A browser shows "no drop" whenever the pointer enters a new element whose `dragenter` event isn't cancelled, until the next `dragover`. We only cancelled `dragover`, so crossing rows, their avatar/name/labels, or the gaps between rows flashed the symbol.
- **Fix:** the list now handles the drag as a whole. While a row is being dragged, it cancels `dragenter` and `dragover` everywhere in the list, gaps included, and the drop goes to the last row the pointer was over.
- **Verified:** every `dragenter` in the list is now accepted. Drag up gives `[bob, me, alice, misc]` and drag down gives `[alice, bob, me, misc]`.

## 2. Files changed (`e31b0315`)

- `CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx`: the list handles the drag; rows only mark which row is under the pointer.
- `CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.scss`: the line is drawn inside the row, above or below.
- `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`: 7 new tests.

`pr-82.md` is updated with the new commit, the bug notes, and 106 tests in total. It's still uncommitted.

## 3. Test results

- **New tests:** the line is above the target when dragging up (including the top row) and below when dragging down; only one row shows it; the whole list accepts the drag, which is what keeps the cursor steady; dropping in a gap works; the line clears when the drag ends; plus a control showing the list doesn't take drags when nothing is being dragged.
- **Old component:** 5 of the 7 fail against it. The other two pass either way: the control, and the clear-on-drag-end check.
- **Results:** `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx` passes all 67. The dropdown, #116, #81 and collab suites pass 297 of 297, and typecheck, eslint and prettier are clean.

## 4. Things I'm unsure about

- **Cursor shape.** jsdom can't show the cursor, so the tests check what controls it: the drag events being accepted. Please confirm by hand that the cursor stays steady while dragging over the list.
- **Gaps.** A drop in a gap between rows goes to the last row you hovered, and the line stays on that row while you're in the gap.

## Decisions log (new entry)

- Drag passed jsdom and a real-browser drop test → **you found the line missing on the top row and the "no drop" cursor flashing; fix both** → `e31b0315`: line drawn inside the row on the landing side; the whole list accepts the drag.

## Tech debt (new entry)

- **Encountered:** headless Edge doesn't draw anything while a native drag is in progress, so screenshots can't be taken mid-drag. I checked the line's styles mid-drag instead, and took the screenshot with the line's style applied by hand.

Phase 6 is otherwise unchanged and still waiting on you: the full check, `pr-82.md`, and your Stryker run followed by the coverage-gap tests.

# Final run-through: coverage, the new tests, and how it fits together

## 1. Are all test cases covered?

**By acceptance criterion: yes.** Every AC from A to I has at least one test whose expected value comes from the AC text or from one of your recorded decisions. Every "nothing changes" test has a control showing the same setup does change when layering is on.

**By line coverage:** I measured the lines #82 added or changed in each source file, against `origin/master`, two ways.

| File | Only our 106 new tests | Whole suite (2528 passing tests) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `element/src/ownership.ts`: the ordering rule | 118/118 lines, 28/28 branches | 118/118, 30/30 |
| `actions/actionCollaboratorVisibility.ts` | 89/89, 8/8 | 89/89, 8/8 |
| `scene/Renderer.ts` | 20/20, 1/1 | same |
| `scene/export.ts` | 28/28 | same |
| `data/index.ts`, `binding.ts`, `appState.ts`, `actions/index.ts` | all covered | all covered |
| `components/App.tsx` | 76/84 (3 paths missed, see below) | **84/84**, 16/16 |
| `element/src/arrows/focus.ts` | 4/12 | **12/12** |
| `scene/visibility.ts`: `getCollaboratorLayerRows` | 27/29, 3/5 branches | 27/29, 3/5 |
| `CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx` | all lines run; 58/62 branches | all lines; 60/64 branches |

The `types.ts` files are left out because they contain only type declarations, which never run.

**What's still uncovered, and why:**

- **Run by older tests, but only with layering off.** The whole suite reaches the three `App.tsx` paths and the `focus.ts` lines through #116, #81 and upstream tests. That proves those paths still work, but not that they _use the layer order_, because those tests never turn layering on. The three paths:
  - `getBindableElements`: the binding hover/suggestion paths;
  - the text-tool container pick;
  - re-targeting an arrow's focus point.
- **Not reached by any test:**
  - Previously seen rows while layering is on (`visibility.ts`). No test session has someone who left the room while layering is on.
  - The menu's name-filter branches: hiding rows, and drag turned off while filtering. The filter only appears at 8 or more collaborators.
  - Two defensive checks for a missing `dataTransfer`. Real browsers always provide one.
- **Phase 2 edge cases** (empty element list, collaborator without an id, and others) are covered by line now, but there are no dedicated tests for them.

All of these are on the list for the coverage pass you planned after Stryker.

## 2. The test code you haven't seen yet

Total: 106 tests, 33 + 67 + 6. You've seen the 33 Phase 2 tests. Below are the Phase 2 fixture change, the 67 editor tests, and the 6 collab tests.

### 2a. The one change to the Phase 2 file after you approved it

Two fixture fixes, made in Phase 3 and reported then. No expected value changed.

```diff
-/** me, alice and bob in the room; alice joined before bob */
+/**
+ * me, alice and bob in the room; alice joined before bob. Like #116's Collab,
+ * the directory records me too (when the room starts), otherwise my
+ * elements would fall into the miscellaneous bucket.
+ */
 const baseState = {
   collaborators: room("me", "alice", "bob"),
-  collaboratorDirectory: directory("alice", "bob"),
+  collaboratorDirectory: directory("me", "alice", "bob"),
 };
```

```diff
-const createRect = (id: string, creatorId?: string) =>
-  newElement({ type: "rectangle", id, x: 0, y: 0, customData: … });
+// readable ids (the constructors' option types don't accept `id`)
+const createRect = (id: string, creatorId?: string) => ({
+  ...newElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0, customData: … }),
+  id,
+});
```

- **The directory now includes "me".** The real app records your own id in the directory when the room starts (`Collab.tsx:536`), and the fixture didn't.
- **Ids are set with a spread.** The typecheck rejects `id` as a constructor option, even though it works at runtime.

### 2b. Editor tests: [collaboratorLayer.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorLayer.test.tsx), 67 tests

**Shared setup.** Every test renders the real editor. It has two overlapping filled squares, `alice-under` and then `bob-over` (Bob on top in the shared order), and three collaborators: me, Alice and Bob. The directory records them in the order me, Alice, Bob, so the default layer order is `[me, alice, bob, misc]`.

```tsx
const stamp = (element, creatorId) =>
  newElementWith(element, { customData: { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId } });

/** solid fill so clicking the interior counts as a hit */
const createSolidRect = (id, extra = {}) =>
  API.createElement({
    type: "rectangle",
    id,
    x: extra.x ?? 0,
    y: extra.y ?? 0,
    width: extra.width ?? 100,
    height: 100,
    backgroundColor: "red",
    fillStyle: "solid",
    strokeColor: extra.strokeColor,
    frameId: extra.frameId ?? null,
    boundElements: extra.boundElements ?? null,
  });

const execute = (name, value?) => {
  // runs a real registered action
  const action = h.app.actionManager.actions[name];
  assert.isDefined(action, `action "${name}" should be registered`);
  act(() => {
    h.app.actionManager.executeAction(action, "ui", value);
  });
};
const toggleLayering = () => execute("toggleCollaboratorLayering");
const move = (id, toIndex) => execute("moveCollaboratorLayer", { id, toIndex });
const layerOrder = () => getCollaboratorLayerOrder(h.state); // top row first
const drawnIds = () => h.app.visibleElements.map((el) => el.id); // what App draws, bottom → top
const getShared = () =>
  h.elements.map(({ id, index, version, versionNonce }) => ({
    id,
    index,
    version,
    versionNonce,
  })); // what AC E says must not change

const DEFAULT_ORDER = ["me", "alice", "bob", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID];

beforeEach(async () => {
  await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
  API.setElements([
    stamp(createSolidRect("alice-under"), "alice"),
    stamp(createSolidRect("bob-over"), "bob"),
  ]);
  act(() => {
    h.app.updateScene({ collaborators }); // me (current user), alice, bob
    API.setAppState({ collaboratorDirectory, width: 1000, height: 1000 }); // jsdom viewport is 0×0
  });
});
```

`drawnIds()` reads `h.app.visibleElements`, which App's real render path fills in. Setting a width and height is what makes jsdom draw anything at all. So these tests check what's actually drawn, not a copy of the logic.

#### Switch, moving and Reset (AC A, B, Reset): 9 tests

```tsx
it("AC-A: the Layering switch is off by default", () => {
  expect(h.state.collaboratorLayeringEnabled).toBe(false);
  expect(h.state.collaboratorLayerOrder).toBe(null);
});
it("default order: the first switch-on puts me on top, then join order, miscellaneous last", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  expect(h.state.collaboratorLayeringEnabled).toBe(true);
  expect(h.state.collaboratorLayerOrder).toEqual(DEFAULT_ORDER);
});
it("AC-A: moving a row one place up", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move("bob", 1);
  expect(layerOrder()).toEqual(["me", "bob", "alice", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID]);
});
it("AC-A: moving a row to a drop position", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move(UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID, 0);
  expect(layerOrder()).toEqual([UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID, "me", "alice", "bob"]);
});
it("AC-A: rows can't be moved while the switch is off (controls hidden)", () => {
  move("bob", 0);
  expect(h.state.collaboratorLayerOrder).toBe(null);
});
it("AC-B: turning the switch off and on again keeps the chosen order", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move("bob", 0);
  toggleLayering();
  expect(h.state.collaboratorLayeringEnabled).toBe(false);
  toggleLayering();
  expect(layerOrder()).toEqual(["bob", "me", "alice", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID]);
});
it("reset: returns to the default order with me on top", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move("me", 3);
  move("bob", 0);
  execute("resetCollaboratorLayerOrder");
  expect(layerOrder()).toEqual(DEFAULT_ORDER);
});
it("reset: does nothing while the switch is off (grayed out)", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move("bob", 0);
  toggleLayering();
  execute("resetCollaboratorLayerOrder");
  expect(h.state.collaboratorLayerOrder).toEqual([
    "bob",
    "me",
    "alice",
    UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
  ]);
});
it("reset: me can be moved down again after a reset", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  execute("resetCollaboratorLayerOrder");
  move("me", 1);
  expect(layerOrder()).toEqual(["alice", "me", "bob", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID]);
});
```

These drive the real actions, not the helper functions:

- The first switch-on stores your join order, and switching off and on keeps any changes (your A1).
- Moves are ignored while the switch is off (AC A: controls hidden).
- Reset returns to "me on top" (your A2), does nothing while the switch is off (your "grayed out"), and you can still move yourself down afterwards (your follow-up point 1).

#### AC B: drawing, plus Bring forward (AC E), 5 tests

```tsx
it("AC-B: with the switch off the canvas uses the shared order, even with a chosen order", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move("alice", 0);
  toggleLayering();
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["alice-under", "bob-over"]);
});
it("AC-B: (control) the same setup with the switch on is drawn differently", () => {

  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["bob-over", "alice-under"]);
});
it("AC-B: every element of a higher collaborator is above every element of a lower one; each keeps the shared order", () => {
  API.setElements([a1(alice), b1(bob), a2(alice), b2(bob)]);
  toggleLayering();
  move("alice", 0);
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["b1", "b2", "a1", "a2"]);
});
it("AC-E: my own Bring forward changes the shared order and takes effect within my layer", () => {
  API.setElements([m1(me), m2(me), a1(alice)]);
  toggleLayering(); // default: me on top
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["a1", "m1", "m2"]);
  API.setSelectedElements([getElement("m1")]);
  execute("bringForward");
```

- **First test:** the "switch off → looks exactly as without the feature" half of AC B. Even with a chosen order stored, switching off draws the shared order. The control right after it shows the same setup draws differently with the switch on.
- **Interleaved test:** a1, b1, a2, b2 become b1, b2, a1, a2. Every Alice element is above every Bob element (AC B part 1), and within each person the shared order is kept, a1 before a2 (AC B part 2).
- **Bring forward:** uses the editor's real `bringForward` action. Your element's shared `index` really changes (AC E: "still change the shared order as before"), but on your screen m1 only moves above m2, inside your own layer. Alice's a1 stays below both.
  - This is the test I fixed in Phase 4 after finding it passed even without the wiring.

#### AC D: attached elements, 5 tests

```tsx
it("AC-D: a label is drawn directly with its container, even when the label's creator is higher", () => {
  API.setElements([ container(alice, boundElements: [label]), bob-shape(bob), label(bob, containerId: container) ]);
  toggleLayering(); move("bob", 0);               // bob on top
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["container", "label", "bob-shape"]);
});
describe("frame children are still clipped", () => {
  // alice's frame (x 0–100) with bob's child sticking out (x 50–150); bob on top
  it("AC-D: (control) layering on does reorder the frame and its child", () =>
    expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["frame", "child"]));
  it("AC-D: the child keeps its frame, so it's still clipped to it", () =>
    expect(getElement("child").frameId).toBe("frame"));
  it("AC-D: clicking the child inside the frame selects it", () => {
    mouse.clickAt(75, 50); expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["child"]); });
  it("AC-D: clicking the child's clipped part outside the frame selects nothing", () => {
    mouse.clickAt(125, 50); expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual([]); });
});
```

- **Label:** the label is stamped by Bob, but its container is Alice's, and Bob is on top. If the label followed its own creator, it would jump to Bob's layer. It stays right after its container: AC D's "even if the label and container have different creators".
- **Frame:** the control shows layering really does reorder the frame and its child. The other three show the clip still holds:
  - the child keeps its frame link (clipping is per element);
  - a click inside the frame selects the child;
  - a click on the part sticking _outside_ the frame hits nothing, because Excalidraw's clip-aware hit test still applies with layering on.

- **Clicks:** all real clicks through the editor's pointer handling. With the switch off, the shared top (Bob) is selected. With it on and Alice above, Alice's square is selected even though it's _under_ Bob in the shared order.

AC E is literal here: `index`, `version` and `versionNonce` are identical before and after every layering action. The scene's own element array, which is what syncs to others, stays in shared order while your canvas draws a different one.

#### AC I: export, 5 tests

```tsx
const ALICE = "#aa0000",
  BOB = "#0000bb"; // distinct stroke colors to find each shape in the SVG
const exportSvg = async () => {
  // the real "copy as SVG" path, clipboard intercepted
  const copy = vi
    .spyOn(Clipboard, "copyTextToSystemClipboard")
    .mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  await exportCanvas(
    "clipboard-svg",
    exportElements(),
    h.state,
    {},
    {
      exportBackground: false,
      viewBackgroundColor: "#ffffff",
      exportingFrame: null,
    },
  );
  const svg = copy.mock.calls[0][0];
  copy.mockRestore();
  return svg;
};
const exportPngDrawOrder = async () => {
  // what the PNG export hands to the renderer
  const renderSpy = vi.spyOn(StaticScene, "renderStaticScene");
  await exportToCanvas(
    exportElements(),
    h.state,
    {},
    { exportBackground: false, viewBackgroundColor: "#ffffff" },
  );
  const drawn = renderSpy.mock.calls[0][0].visibleElements.map((el) => el.id);
  renderSpy.mockRestore();
  return drawn;
};
it("AC-I: (control) with the switch off, the SVG export uses the shared order", async () => {
  const svg = await exportSvg();
  expect(svg.indexOf(ALICE)).toBeLessThan(svg.indexOf(BOB));
});
it("AC-I: the SVG export follows my layer order", async () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move("alice", 0);
  const svg = await exportSvg();
  expect(svg.indexOf(BOB)).toBeLessThan(svg.indexOf(ALICE));
});
it("AC-I: (control) with the switch off, the PNG export uses the shared order", async () =>
  expect(await exportPngDrawOrder()).toEqual(["alice-under", "bob-over"]));
it("AC-I: the PNG export follows my layer order", async () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move("alice", 0);
  expect(await exportPngDrawOrder()).toEqual(["bob-over", "alice-under"]);
});
it("AC-E: exporting with layering on changes no element index or version", async () => {
  toggleLayering();
  move("alice", 0);
  const before = getShared();
  await exportPngDrawOrder();
  await exportSvg();
  expect(getShared()).toEqual(before);
});
```

- **SVG:** goes through the editor's real `exportCanvas("clipboard-svg")`, so the wiring that passes the layering fields along is tested too. In SVG, document order is drawing order: whichever color appears later is drawn on top.
- **PNG:** checks the exact list the canvas exporter draws, by spying on the real renderer.
- **The last test guards the export trap.** The PNG export rewrites element indices if it's given a reordered list (`syncInvalidIndices`). Exporting with layering on must still leave every index and version unchanged.

**While dragging: drop line and cursor (7).** These are the tests for the two bugs you found.

```tsx
const enter = (el) => fireEvent.dragEnter(el, { dataTransfer }); // returns false when the list accepted it
it("AC-A: dragging up shows the drop line above the target, including the top row", () => {
  startDrag("bob"); enter(getRowElement("me"));
  expect(getRowElement("me").classList).toContain("is-drop-above"); /* and not below */ });

  expect(enter(getList())).toBe(true));

  expect(enter(getList())).toBe(false);                 // a gap between rows
  expect(enter(getRowElement("alice"))).toBe(false);    // a row

  expect(fireEvent.dragOver(getList(), { dataTransfer })).toBe(false);

it("AC-A: the drop line goes away when the drag ends", …no is-drop-* class);
```

- **Testing the cursor without a cursor.** jsdom has no cursor, so these test what decides it. `fireEvent` returns `false` when the event was cancelled, which in a real browser means "a drop is allowed here", so no "no drop" symbol.
- **Coverage of the cursor fix:** the gap, a row and a row's contents. Those are exactly the elements whose `dragenter` produced the flash.
- **Control:** without a drag in progress, the list doesn't take drops, so canvas file drops still go to the canvas.
- **Shown to catch the bugs:** 5 of the 7 failed against the component from before the fix.

### 2c. Collab tests: [collabLayer.test.tsx](excalidraw-app/tests/collabLayer.test.tsx), 6 tests

**Setup.** The real `ExcalidrawApp` with the real `Collab` and `Portal` classes. The socket is a recorder: every message the client sends is captured, and incoming messages are injected. Encryption is a passthrough and Firebase is stubbed. Each test starts a room and receives a peer's element, `theirs`. These mocks are about 60 lines copied from `collabLock.test.tsx` and not repeated here.

```tsx
const reorderLocally = () => {              // layering on, miscellaneous (alice: unseen → misc) on top
  execute("toggleCollaboratorLayering");
  execute("moveCollaboratorLayer", { id: UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID, toIndex: 0 });
};

it("(control) a local edit is sent to the room", async () => {
  const sentBefore = getSentUpdates().length;
  addLocalElement("mine");
  await waitFor(() => expect(getSentElementIdsSince(sentBefore)[0]).toContain("mine"));
});

it("(control) the same reorder does change my local drawing order", () => {
  /* add "mine", stamped with my real client id, on top of "theirs" */
  API.setAppState({ width: 1000, height: 1000 });
  expect(h.app.visibleElements.map((el) => el.id)).toEqual(["theirs", "mine"]);
  reorderLocally();
  expect(h.app.visibleElements.map((el) => el.id)).toEqual(["mine", "theirs"]);
});

it("AC-E: switching layering, reordering and resetting send nothing new to other collaborators", async () => {
  const sentBefore = getSentUpdates().length;
  const emittedBefore = mocks.emitted.length;
  reorderLocally(); execute("resetCollaboratorLayerOrder"); execute("toggleCollaboratorLayering");
  sync();                                   // what onChange would do
  addLocalElement("marker");
  await waitFor(() => expect(getSentUpdates().length).toBeGreaterThan(sentBefore));
  expect(getSentElementIdsSince(sentBefore)[0]).toContain("marker");
  expect(mocks.emitted.slice(emittedBefore).findIndex(([event]) => event === WS_EVENTS.SERVER)).toBe(0);
});

it("AC-E: reordering changes no element index or version", () => {
  const before = getShared(); reorderLocally(); sync();
  expect(getShared()).toEqual(before);
});

it("AC-E: a local edit while reordered sends the shared indices", async () => {
  reorderLocally();
  const sharedIndex = getElement("theirs").index;
  /* add "marker", wait for the send */
  const sentTheirs = /* "theirs" in what was sent, if anything */;
  expect(sentTheirs?.index ?? sharedIndex).toBe(sharedIndex);
});

it("AC-E: a peer's update still arrives, and my scene keeps the shared order", async () => {
  reorderLocally();
  await receivePeerElement("theirs-2");
  const indices = h.elements.map((el) => el.index!);
  expect(indices).toEqual([...indices].sort());
  expect(h.elements.map((el) => el.id)).toEqual(["theirs", "theirs-2"]);
});
```

- **Two controls:**
  - the recorder really does capture sends (a normal edit shows up);
  - in _this_ collab session the reorder really does change your local drawing. So the "nothing sent / nothing changed" tests below can't pass just because nothing happened.
- **The marker technique**, the same one #81 used. Messages go out in order, so if the first update sent after all the layering actions is the marker edit, the layering actions themselves sent nothing. The `findIndex(...) === 0` line also rules out other messages, such as volatile ones, going out in between.
- **"Sends the shared indices":** even when you edit something while reordered, any copy of a peer's element that goes out carries its original shared `index`.
- **Peer updates:** a peer's new element still arrives while you're reordered, and your scene, the data that syncs, stays sorted by shared index. So other collaborators see the shared order (AC E).

## 3. How the new parts flow and plug into #116, #81 and base Excalidraw


**Walking through one session:**

1. **The dropdown dispatches actions.** The switch, arrows, drag and Reset only dispatch actions. They sit next to #116's and #81's in the same file and use the same pattern: `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER`, so no history entry and nothing to sync.
2. **The state lives beside #116's and #81's.** The two new fields are configured exactly like `lockedCollaboratorIds`, so Excalidraw's existing filters for local storage, export and the server drop them automatically.
3. **The order is built from existing data.** The default order reads #116's `collaboratorDirectory`, which `Collab.tsx` already fills as people are seen. The current user comes from base Excalidraw's `collaborators` map, the same way #81 finds "me". No new collaboration code was needed.
4. **One function makes every decision.** `orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer` uses #116's bucket rule, so labels follow their containers and untagged or never-seen creators go to Miscellaneous. It's a stable sort, so each person keeps the shared order. While the switch is off it returns the _same array_, so the off path costs nothing and changes nothing.
5. **Every "what's on top" path calls it.**
   - **The renderer** orders before its memoized map, so base Excalidraw's static scene draws in layer order. Its existing rules then apply unchanged: labels drawn with their container, frame clip per element, masks.
   - **Hit-testing** orders first. #81's interactivity filter then removes locked or hidden elements, and Excalidraw's own frame-clip and mask rules follow. The last remaining hit is what's on top on your screen. That's why "click through a locked top element" works without new code.
   - **Binding** gets the same ordered list, both through #116's `getBindableElements` and through the two element-package chokepoints, where #116's hidden filter is applied first.
   - **Export** applies #116's visibility filter first (`prepareElementsForExport`, unchanged), then layers only the list to draw, inside the existing `prepareElementsForRender`. That's after the index sync and outside the embedded scene data.
6. **Shared data is never written.** The scene array, fractional indices, z-order actions, Collab sync and history are all untouched. That's what the AC E tests (editor and collab) and the export index test lock in.
7. **Performance.** `getLocalLayerOrder()` keeps the same array while the order's contents are unchanged. Peers' cursor updates replace `collaborators` many times a second, and this stops them from invalidating the renderer and hit-test caches.

**Next step, as planned:** your Stryker run on the changed source files. Then a final pass adding tests for the gaps listed in section 1. Nothing is pushed, and `pr-82.md` is still uncommitted.

The 3 failures don't need fixing in #82, and they won't fail CI. They only fail on Windows, because of how the test setup finds font files. With that worked around temporarily, the whole suite passes on our branch: 159 of 159 test files, 0 failures, with the saved snapshots unchanged. My earlier guess that they came from "the recent font work" was wrong, and you were right to push back.

**Why they fail here and not in CI**

- The test setup (`setupTests.ts`) builds the path to the font files as `file://${__dirname}/`.
- On Windows, the build tool resolves each font to a `/@fs/C:/Users/...` path, and that base turns it into a file that doesn't exist.
- Every font read fails (`ENOENT`), so the SVG export points to fonts by web address instead of embedding them, and the 3 snapshots no longer match.
- CI runs on Linux (`ubuntu-latest`), where the same path finds the real file. `master`'s CI has passed on every recent merge, including #178.

**Proof that our code isn't involved**

1. On the exact current `master` code, on this machine, the same 3 tests fail.
2. I temporarily patched the setup's font reader so it finds the real files on Windows, and ran:

   - the full suite: 159 of 159 files, 2532 tests, 0 failures.
3. I reverted the patch and left the snapshots alone. If they were regenerated on Windows, they would break CI on Linux.

The full run also warns about one obsolete snapshot (`with a CJK font 2`). Master's #178 added it, our branch doesn't touch that file, and it doesn't fail runs.

```text
Implement Group-Project Element Functionality
CLOSED
# Issue Description

## Summary

Implement support for group projects and shared ownership in collaborative editing sessions.

When multiple peers edit or contribute to the same element or drawing cluster, the system must recognize and assign joint ownership to all participating collaborators. Consequently, visibility and control states must adapt such that a shared item remains visible if any of its co-owners are set to be visible. This feature ensures seamless tracking of collaborative co-creation without disrupting independent element management.

## User Story

**As a** user, **I want** elements edited by multiple peers to be jointly owned and dynamically visible when any contributing peer is visible **so that** co-created work in group projects is never prematurely hidden or broken.

## User Scenario

A team of students is working together on a collaborative design. Two peers simultaneously contribute to and modify a core diagram element, making it a co-edited asset owned by both. When another user toggles visibility for one of the co-authors, the shared diagram element remains visible because at least one of its active joint owners is currently visible, ensuring continuous context for the group project.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium

**Specific:** Greater Medium (8 points)

**Reason:** Requires updating the ownership tracking model to support multi-peer shared elements, adjusting visibility evaluation logic for co-edited objects, and synchronizing group project state across clients.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Criteria A: Joint ownership tracking.** The system correctly identifies and registers multiple collaborators as co-owners of an element or drawing cluster when edits or contributions overlap.
- [ ] **Criteria B: Shared visibility evaluation.** An element with joint ownership remains visible on the local client as long as at least one of its co-owners has their visibility enabled.
- [ ] **Criteria C: Dynamic ownership updates.** When new collaborators edit an existing element, ownership dynamically expands to include them without corrupting historical state.

## Open Question

- How should ownership precedence or fallback behave if all co-owners of a group project element are hidden simultaneously?
- How should merge conflicts or simultaneous competing edits be resolved when establishing joint ownership?
- Should joint ownership persist if one of the co-authors deletes their direct contributions from the element?

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

- Automated AI-driven merging of conflicting drawing paths or shapes.
- Server-side access control lists restricting who is allowed to join a group project.
- Permanent locking of group project elements to specific subsets of users.

## Head Issue

Issue (#14): Allow a togglable Layer in which all users are compartmentalized by interactivity and visibility.
```
