```text
Closes #84

## Why

Issue #84 (child of #14). Hiding and locking collaborators (#81) was based only on who *created* an element. Once someone edited another person's element, the element still followed only its creator's visibility and lock settings, so a collaborator you had chosen to keep visible could have their work hidden or locked away. This issue makes everyone who edits an element its co-owner, and makes the element follow the least restricted of its owners: it stays visible, and editable, as long as at least one co-owner is.

Working through how co-ownership behaves in a live room exposed several sync problems, which this PR also fixes:
- Conflicting edits were decided by "the copy changed the most times wins", so a long drag beat a later delete.
- Concurrent co-owner stamps could overwrite each other.
- Changes from other users made during your drag, resize or text edit were silently dropped.
- Elements whose deletion was older than 24 hours could come back.

## What changed

- **Co-ownership data:** `customData.creatorId` still records the creator. New fields:
  - `customData.editorIds`: the current co-owners.
  - `customData.editorSeqs`: a counter per client, bumped each time that client is added or removed. It makes the co-owner list mergeable: only each client changes its own entry, so the higher counter is the newer state, and a removed co-owner keeps their counter as a marker so an older copy can't add them back.
- **Becoming a co-owner (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`, `packages/element/src/store.ts`, `App.tsx`):**
  - A new `Store.onBeforeDurableCaptureEmitter` fires just before a local change is saved to undo history.
  - At that point, `getElementsToCoOwn` finds elements the user edited directly (selected, or text being edited) but doesn't own, and stamps the user as a co-owner as part of the **same undo step**.
  - Side effects don't count: rerouted arrows, frame children, z-order, `boundElements`.
  - Editing a label co-owns its shape.
- **Least-restricted-owner rule:**
  - `isElementByHiddenCreator`: an element is hidden only if **every** owner is hidden.
  - `isElementInteractive`: it can be interacted with if **any** owner is interactive.

  Rendering, hit testing, selection, the eraser, export, search and arrow binding all go through these two functions, so all of them follow the new rule. "Hide all" and the per-row drawing counts include co-owners.
- **Undo/redo (`packages/excalidraw/history.ts`):**
  - Undoing every edit a user made to an element removes them as a co-owner; redo adds them back.
  - Undo/redo normally restores the whole `customData` object. A merge step now keeps other clients' co-ownership as it was, so only the current user's entry follows history.
- **Latest change wins (`packages/common/src/clock.ts`, `packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts`):**
  - A hybrid logical clock stamps `updated`: it follows the wall clock, never goes backwards, has a logical counter for changes within the same millisecond, and jumps forward when it sees a newer remote timestamp (capped at 60 s ahead of the local clock).
  - It's stored in the same `updated` number as `ms + counter/1024`, so the format doesn't change.
  - Reconcile now keeps the copy with the later timestamp. It falls back to the old version/nonce rules for same-millisecond changes and for old data without timestamps.
  - Co-owner lists are merged from both copies instead of being taken from the winner.
- **Incoming changes during edits in progress (new module `packages/excalidraw/data/inProgressEdit.ts`):**
  - Covers resizing or rotating one element, text editing, drawing a new element, dragging, and multi-element transforms.
  - Each edit owns some properties: geometry for all of them, plus the text for a text edit and `frameId` for a drag. A newer remote change to any *other* property is merged into the local element. For example, a recolour made during your drag survives.
  - A newer remote delete:
    - **text edit, single-element resize, drawing, multi-element transform:** cancels the edit;
    - **drag:** removes just that element, and the rest keep moving.

    Either way, the editor re-issues the delete with a later timestamp so it sticks, and shows a notice.
  - Stale copies made before the edit started are ignored.
  - To support cancelling, the text editor now returns `{ submit, cancel }`, and `App` keeps a reference to the active pointer gesture.
- **Expired deletions (new module `excalidraw-app/collab/expiredDeletions.ts`):** deleted elements stop syncing 24 hours after deletion.
  - **The rule:** a live element the room's stored scene doesn't have, which this client synced before, and which hasn't changed in over 24 hours, was deleted.
  - **When saving to Firebase:** such elements are left out of the save and deleted locally.
  - **When receiving an update:** old live elements this client doesn't have are ignored. Age is measured with the sender's clock, via a new optional `sentAt` field on scene updates, so a client whose clock is far behind can still add elements.
- **Strings:** `collaboratorEdit.deletedWhileEditing` added to `en.json`.

## Tech Debt

### Introduced

- **One edit per page:** the in-progress-edit registry (`inProgressEdit.ts`) and the element clock (`elementClock`) are module-level singletons. Two Excalidraw editors on the same page would share them.
- **Co-owner removal markers are never cleaned up.** `editorSeqs` keeps an entry for every client that ever co-owned an element.
- **Fractional timestamps:** `updated` can now have a fractional part. External tools that assume whole milliseconds will see fractions. The encoding is exact until about the year 2248.
- **Deploy all clients together:** clients running the old rule and the new rule can settle on different copies of a conflicting element. Reloading the page fixes it.
- **Edits not covered by the in-progress handling:** line/arrow point editing, cropping and arrow-key nudges still use plain "latest change wins". During those continuous edits, remote changes are mostly lost.
- **Cancelling an edit loses work:**
  - Cancelling a multi-element transform leaves the other elements where they were mid-gesture. Nothing is rolled back, and they're only recorded in undo with the next change.
  - Cancelling a text edit loses the text typed so far.
- **The delete notice doesn't say who deleted the element**, and the new string is in `en.json` only.
- **Expiry false positive:** a live element whose Firebase saves failed for over 24 hours can be treated as an expired deletion. Some peers may not see it until the next successful save brings it back.
- **Clock skew isn't solved:** changes made at the same time on two devices whose clocks disagree, before they've exchanged anything, are still ordered by those clocks. The 60 s cap limits how far a wrong clock can push others.

### Encountered

- **Arrow-key moves aren't saved as their own undo step;** they're folded into the next one. This also delays co-ownership from an arrow-key move until that next step.
- **The text editor and pointer gestures had no way to cancel.** Both were added for this PR.
- **`getUpdatedTimestamp()` returns `1` in tests.** Every existing test therefore runs on the version fallback, and the new time-ordering tests set timestamps explicitly.
- **Test failures not caused by this PR:**
  - `pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx` (an untracked file in the working tree, not part of this PR) was already failing before this work.
  - `pathMotionConfig.test.tsx` ("a 300px path at 0.5x speed plays for 2000ms") and `history.test.tsx` ("should create new history entry on scene import via drag&drop") failed once each under full-suite load and passed when run alone.
- **Remote updates during a gesture update the store snapshot mid-gesture,** so that gesture's undo step can be partial. This was already the case for drags and is unchanged by this PR.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Joint ownership tracking | `coOwnership.test.tsx`: "editing a collaborator's element adds me as a co-owner, keeping the creator", "selecting without editing doesn't", "editing my own element doesn't add me as a co-owner", "a co-owned element counts for each owner in the menu"; `coOwnership.test.ts` (element): "a selected, edited element someone else created gets me as co-owner", "an element changed as a side effect (not selected) doesn't", "elements I already own don't", "new, deleted, unstamped or merely re-indexed elements don't", "editing a label co-owns its shape", "does nothing outside of a room (no self id)", "moving or restyling is an edit", "bookkeeping, z-order and binding references are not", "lists the creator first, then co-owners, without duplicates", "bound text follows its container's owners", "keeps concurrent co-owners from both copies", "is commutative: both orders give the same co-owners"; `reconcileClock.test.ts`: "concurrent co-owner stamps both survive, whichever copy wins" | unit, integration | AC, issue discussion |
| B: Shared visibility evaluation | `coOwnership.test.tsx` › "visibility of a co-owned element (rendering, AC-B)": "(control) without co-owners, hiding the creator hides the element", "after I edit it, hiding its creator keeps it on my canvas and in exports", "it's hidden once every one of its co-owners is hidden", "a peer's co-owned element stays visible while any co-owner is visible", "shows again as soon as one co-owner is shown again"; also "once I co-own it, locking its creator doesn't lock it for me", "without co-owning, locking its creator deselects it (unchanged)"; `coOwnership.test.ts` › "least restricted owner rule" (7 tests, including "Bob locked, Carol not → interactive for Alice" and "Bob hidden, Carol visible → visible and interactive") | unit, integration | AC, issue discussion (the Alice/Bob/Carol example) |

**Not tested automatically, and why:**
- No criterion was checked only by hand, and no manual checks were done.
- Real collaboration between two browsers (relay server and Firebase) isn't covered. The tests apply remote updates through `reconcileElements` or `updateScene` directly, so Collab, Portal and the socket/Firebase code paths aren't exercised.
- Groups as "drawing clusters" (AC-A) have no dedicated test. Co-ownership is per element, so editing a group stamps each edited member, but no test checks that.
- The expiry rules are unit-tested, but their wiring into `Collab.tsx` and `firebase.ts` is not. No test simulates a tab offline for more than 24 hours.
```

```text
import { arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { isBoundToContainer } from "./typeChecks";

import type { ElementsMap, ExcalidrawElement } from "./types";

/** `customData` key holding the id of the client that created the element */
export const CREATOR_ID_KEY = "creatorId";

/**
 * `customData` key holding the ids of the clients that edited an element they
 * didn't create (co-owners). The element follows the least restrictive
 * visibility/lock setting among its creator and co-owners.
 */
export const EDITOR_IDS_KEY = "editorIds";

/**
 * `customData` key holding, per client that ever co-owned the element, a
 * counter bumped each time that client is added or removed. It turns the
 * co-owner list into a mergeable set: every client only ever changes its own
 * entry, so when copies disagree the higher counter is the newer state. Ids
 * listed here but not in `editorIds` were removed (kept so a stale copy can't
 * bring them back).
 */
export const EDITOR_SEQS_KEY = "editorSeqs";

/** bucket for elements without (valid) creator metadata, e.g. legacy rooms */
export const UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID = "__unknown__";

const getStampedCreatorId = (element: ExcalidrawElement): string | null => {
  const creatorId = element.customData?.[CREATOR_ID_KEY];
  return typeof creatorId === "string" && creatorId ? creatorId : null;
};

/** the element's current co-owners: valid, de-duplicated ids */
export const getStampedEditorIds = (element: ExcalidrawElement): string[] => {
  const editorIds = element.customData?.[EDITOR_IDS_KEY];
  if (!Array.isArray(editorIds)) {
    return [];
  }
  return [
    ...new Set(
      editorIds.filter(
        (id: unknown): id is string => typeof id === "string" && !!id,
      ),
    ),
  ];
};

/** the element holding `element`'s ownership (bound text → its container) */
const getOwnershipHolder = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): ExcalidrawElement =>
  isBoundToContainer(element)
    ? elementsMap.get(element.containerId) ?? element
    : element;

/**
 * Returns the id of the client that created the element, or
 * `UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID` if it isn't known.
 *
 * Bound text follows its container so labels never show/hide separately
 * from the shape they belong to.
 */
export const getElementCreatorId = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): string =>
  getStampedCreatorId(getOwnershipHolder(element, elementsMap)) ??
  UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID;

/**
 * Every owner of the element: its creator (or `UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID` if not
 * known) followed by its co-owners. Bound text follows its container.
 */
export const getElementOwnerIds = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): string[] => {
  const holder = getOwnershipHolder(element, elementsMap);
  return [
    ...new Set([
      getStampedCreatorId(holder) ?? UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
      ...getStampedEditorIds(holder),
    ]),
  ];
};

/** structurally satisfied by the editor's AppState */
export type CreatorVisibility = {
  /**
   * creator ids hidden on this client. `UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID` hides the
   * miscellaneous bucket.
   */
  hiddenCollaboratorIds?: ReadonlySet<string>;
  /**
   * creators this client can name (seen at some point). Stamped creators
   * missing from it are treated as unknown (miscellaneous). `null`/omitted
   * (e.g. outside of a room) → every stamped creator is its own bucket.
   */
  collaboratorDirectory?: ReadonlyMap<string, unknown> | null;
};

/** an owner's bucket: `UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID` if this client never saw them */
const toVisibilityBucket = (
  ownerId: string,
  collaboratorDirectory: CreatorVisibility["collaboratorDirectory"],
): string =>
  collaboratorDirectory &&
  ownerId !== UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID &&
  !collaboratorDirectory.has(ownerId)
    ? UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID
    : ownerId;

/**
 * The visibility bucket of the element's creator: the creator, or
 * `UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID` for untagged elements and creators this client has
 * never seen. Ignores co-owners; see `getElementVisibilityBuckets`.
 */
export const getElementVisibilityBucket = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
  collaboratorDirectory: CreatorVisibility["collaboratorDirectory"],
): string =>
  toVisibilityBucket(
    getElementCreatorId(element, elementsMap),
    collaboratorDirectory,
  );

/**
 * Every visibility bucket the element belongs to: its creator's and each
 * co-owner's (de-duplicated, so several unknown owners share one bucket).
 */
export const getElementVisibilityBuckets = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
  collaboratorDirectory: CreatorVisibility["collaboratorDirectory"],
): string[] => [
  ...new Set(
    getElementOwnerIds(element, elementsMap).map((ownerId) =>
      toVisibilityBucket(ownerId, collaboratorDirectory),
    ),
  ),
];

/**
 * Whether the element is hidden: only when EVERY one of its visibility
 * buckets is hidden (it follows its least restricted owner).
 *
 * Element-level counterpart of the editor's `isElementHiddenLocally`, so
 * element logic (selection, binding) can exclude hidden collaborators'
 * elements without depending on the editor package.
 */
export const isElementByHiddenCreator = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
  { hiddenCollaboratorIds, collaboratorDirectory }: CreatorVisibility,
): boolean => {
  if (!hiddenCollaboratorIds?.size) {
    return false;
  }
  return getElementVisibilityBuckets(
    element,
    elementsMap,
    collaboratorDirectory,
  ).every((bucketId) => hiddenCollaboratorIds.has(bucketId));
};

/** structurally satisfied by the editor's AppState */
export type CreatorInteractivity = CreatorVisibility & {
  /**
   * creator ids locked on this client (visible but non-interactive).
   * `UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID` locks the miscellaneous bucket.
   */
  lockedCollaboratorIds?: ReadonlySet<string>;
};

/**
 * The interactivity rule (#81): whether this client may interact with a
 * visibility bucket's elements.
 *
 * - hidden → never interactive (no interactivity without visibility)
 * - your own bucket → can't be locked
 * - otherwise → interactive unless locked
 */
export const isCollaboratorInteractive = (
  bucketId: string,
  { hiddenCollaboratorIds, lockedCollaboratorIds }: CreatorInteractivity,
  selfId: string | null,
): boolean => {
  if (hiddenCollaboratorIds?.has(bucketId)) {
    return false;
  }
  if (bucketId === selfId) {
    return true;
  }
  return !lockedCollaboratorIds?.has(bucketId);
};
```

```text
/**
 * Whether this client may interact with the element (select, move, resize,
 * rotate, delete, erase, text-edit): when ANY of its visibility buckets is
 * interactive per `isCollaboratorInteractive`, i.e. it follows its least
 * restricted owner. Elements whose buckets are all hidden never are.
 *
 * @param selfId defaults to the current user's id from `state.collaborators`;
 * pass it when checking many elements.
 */
export const isElementInteractive = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
  state: CreatorInteractivity & CreatorSelf,
  selfId: string | null = getSelfCreatorId(state),
): boolean =>
  getElementVisibilityBuckets(
    element,
    elementsMap,
    state.collaboratorDirectory,
  ).some((bucketId) => isCollaboratorInteractive(bucketId, state, selfId));

/**
 * Filters out elements this client may not interact with (hidden or locked
 * collaborators'). Returns the input array as-is when nobody is hidden or
 * locked.
 *
 * @param elementsMap used to resolve bound text containers. Defaults to a map
 * of `elements`, so pass the full scene map when `elements` is a subset.
 */
export const excludeNonInteractiveElements = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  state: CreatorInteractivity & CreatorSelf,
  elementsMap?: ElementsMap,
): readonly T[] => {
  if (
    !state.hiddenCollaboratorIds?.size &&
    !state.lockedCollaboratorIds?.size
  ) {
    return elements;
  }
  const map = elementsMap ?? arrayToMap(elements);
  const selfId = getSelfCreatorId(state);
  return elements.filter((element) =>
    isElementInteractive(element, map, state, selfId),
  );
};

/**
 * Filters out elements whose visibility bucket is hidden. Returns the input
 * array as-is when nothing is hidden.
 *
 * @param elementsMap used to resolve bound text containers. Defaults to a map
 * of `elements`, so pass the full scene map when `elements` is a subset.
 */
export const excludeElementsByHiddenCreators = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  visibility: CreatorVisibility,
  elementsMap?: ElementsMap,
): readonly T[] => {
  if (!visibility.hiddenCollaboratorIds?.size) {
    return elements;
  }
  const map = elementsMap ?? arrayToMap(elements);
  return elements.filter(
    (element) => !isElementByHiddenCreator(element, map, visibility),
  );
};

// co-ownership: editing someone else's element makes you a co-owner

 * other elements (e.g. binding an arrow updates the shape's `boundElements`).
```

#84 is now in `master` (PR #170, merged together with #178). I tested the integration with a trial merge, now discarded. The feature branch is unchanged; nothing was committed or pushed.

## What #84 changes, and where it touches #82

**#84 adds joint ownership.**

- **Who owns an element:** editing someone else's element makes you a co-owner. The ids are stored in a new `customData.editorIds` field next to #116's `creatorId`.
- **The "least restricted owner" rule:** an element is hidden only if _every_ owner is hidden, and is interactive if _any_ owner is.
- **Sync changes** (no overlap with our code):
  - conflicting edits are now decided by the latest timestamp;
  - changes from others during an in-progress edit are merged into it;
  - deleted elements stop syncing after 24 hours.
- **#178 (pages)** comes in with the same merge; I covered it earlier.

**Trial merge results:**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Conflicts | One, in `en.json`: both sides added a string group in the same spot. Fix: keep both. |
| `ownership.ts`, `App.tsx`, `scene/visibility.ts` | Merged automatically. Our code and #84's code don't overlap. |
| Typecheck, lint | clean |
| Full suite (with the temporary Windows font fix) | 164 of 164 files pass, 2629 tests, 0 failures, including our 106 and #84's new tests |

**What carries over with no changes from us:**

- **AC C, click-through.** Our hit test orders first, then applies the interactivity rule. Clicking already follows #84: a co-owned element on top is clickable if any owner is unlocked.
- **The dropdown rows and drawing counts.** They come from #116's row builder, which #84 updated to count co-owners, so the layered list shows the new counts.
- **AC E, nothing shared changes.** #84 only adds co-owners when a change is saved to undo history. Our layering actions never save to undo history, and z-order changes (Bring forward and so on) don't count as edits. Our AC E tests still pass.
- **AC F (local only) and the collab tests.** Still pass with #84's sync changes.

## The decision I need from you

Our layer sort ranks each element by `getElementVisibilityBucket`. After #84, that function deliberately returns the **creator only**. So a co-owned element is drawn in its creator's layer, ignoring its co-owners.

AC B was written when every element had one owner: "every element from a higher collaborator is drawn above every element from a lower one". With co-owned elements that sentence is ambiguous, and per your rules I'm asking rather than reinterpreting it. Example: Bob created a shape, Alice edited it, so both own it.

| Option | Where the co-owned shape is drawn | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Creator only** (what happens if we change nothing) | Bob's layer | Simplest. But if Bob is hidden and the shape stays visible because of Alice (#84), it's drawn in a hidden person's slot. |
| **B. Highest owner** | The higher of Bob's and Alice's layers | Follows #84's "least restricted owner" idea. A hidden owner still counts. |
| **C. Highest visible owner (recommended)** | The higher of the owners who are currently _visible_ | Matches #84 exactly: the shape is drawn in the layer of whoever makes it visible. If Bob is hidden it's drawn in Alice's layer, and when Bob is shown again it moves back up (AC G's "drawn in that place when shown again"). |

## What changes for B or C

**Flow:**

- **The ordering function** (`orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer`): rank by the best of `getElementVisibilityBuckets` (#84's plural function) instead of the creator's bucket alone. For C, it also skips hidden buckets. Labels already follow their container's owners through #84's code.
- **Everything else stays the same.** Rendering, hit-testing, binding and export already call this one function, so they all follow the new rule automatically.
- **Extra cache and export wiring, C only:**
  - App's cached drawing order must also refresh when the hidden list changes. The renderer's cache already does.
  - The SVG export must also pass `hiddenCollaboratorIds`.

**Tests:**

- **None of the existing tests need changing.** Every current test element has a single owner, so they pass under A, B or C.
- **New unit tests** in `ownershipLayer.test.ts):
  - a co-owned element is drawn in its highest (visible) owner's layer;
  - with that owner hidden, it moves to the next visible owner's layer (C);
  - a label on a co-owned shape follows the shape's owners;
  - a single-owner control;
  - the "all owners hidden" fallback.
- **New editor tests** in `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`. I'll make the co-owner the way #84 does: by actually editing Bob's shape as me, not by setting the data directly. Then:
  - it's drawn in the right layer;
  - a click on the overlap selects it;
  - the export draws it in the same order;
  - hiding or showing the owner moves it as expected (C).
- **Expected values** for these come from your decision here plus AC B and AC G. In the PR table they'd be "Other (explain)", or "issue discussion" if you post the amendment on #82, as you did for #81's AC E.

## Proposed order once you decide

1. **Commit 4:** merge `master` (#178 + #84), keeping both string groups in `en.json`.
2. **Commit 5:** co-owned layering (if you choose B or C), with its tests.
3. Full check (typecheck, lint, full suite), then update `pr-82.md`: commit list, tech debt, test table and list, and the decisions log.

Which option do you want: A, B or C? And should commit 5 be its own commit as above, or folded into the merge commit?

```text
1	Closes #82 (Sub-issue of #14)
2
3	## Why
4
5	In a busy room, one collaborator's drawing can end up buried under someone else's large shapes. The shared drawing order (`index`) belongs to everyone, so changing it to fix my view would change it for the whole room. #116 lets me hide collaborators and #81 lets me lock them, but neither changes what is drawn on top.
6
7	This PR adds **local layering**. I can put collaborators in the order their drawings are layered on *my* screen, without touching the shared order or what anyone else sees. It follows the Design comment on #82: a **Layering** switch in the collaborator dropdown. While it's off, nothing changes. While it's on, each row gets **↑ · ↓** controls and the row order is the layer order (top row drawn on top).
8
9	It builds on #116 (ownership via `customData.creatorId`, the rules in `element/ownership.ts`, the dropdown, and the collaborator directory) and #81 (the interactivity rule, locking).
10
11	## What changed
12
13	### The rule (one pure function)
14
15	`orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer` in `packages/element/src/ownership.ts`:
16	- While layering is off, it returns the input array as is.
17	- While it's on, it does a stable sort by each element's layer rank. A higher row is drawn above every element of a lower row, and each collaborator keeps the shared order.
18	- Bound text follows its container: it reuses #116's `getElementVisibilityBucket`, so labels stay with their shapes and untagged or never-seen creators fall into the miscellaneous bucket.
19	- Buckets not in the order go below everyone.
20	- It never changes an element.
21
22	Pure helpers next to it:
23	- `getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder`: me on top, then everyone in **join order**, then miscellaneous last. Join order is the insertion order of #116's `collaboratorDirectory`, so no new tracking was needed.
24	- `getCollaboratorLayerOrder`: the stored order, with newcomers added to the bottom (AC H). Ids are never dropped, so collaborators who are hidden or have left keep their place (AC G).
25	- `moveCollaboratorLayer`: move to a position, clamped; used by the arrows and by drag.
26
27	### State and actions
28
29	- `AppState.collaboratorLayeringEnabled` (default `false`) and `AppState.collaboratorLayerOrder` (default `null`).
30	  - Both are set to `browser`/`export`/`server` `false`, like #81's `lockedCollaboratorIds`. They are never persisted, exported, or synced, and they reset on reload (AC F).
31	- New actions, all with `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` (no history, nothing to sync):
32	  - `toggleCollaboratorLayering`: the first switch-on stores the default order; switching off keeps it.
33	  - `moveCollaboratorLayer` and `resetCollaboratorLayerOrder`: both only work while layering is on.
34
35	### Every "what's on top" path uses the same function
36
37	So what's drawn, what's clicked, what an arrow binds to, and what's exported always agree.
38
39	- **Canvas** (`scene/Renderer.ts`): orders the elements before its memoized element map. The layer order is part of the memo key; the option is optional, so #116's callers are unchanged.
40	- **Hit-testing** (`App.tsx`): `getElementsAtPosition` and the text-container pick use `getElementsInDrawingOrder()`, which is cached per scene change and layer order. #81's click-through to the next interactive element still works.
41	  - `getLocalLayerOrder()` returns the same array while the order's contents don't change, so peers' cursor updates (which replace `collaborators`) don't invalidate the caches.
42	- **Arrow binding**: #116's `getBindableElements()` (all App binding call sites) and the `binding.ts`/`focus.ts` chokepoints use the drawing order, so an arrow binds to the shape on top on my screen.
43	- **PNG/SVG export** (AC I): ordered inside the existing `prepareElementsForRender`, with no new export function. It runs *after* `exportToCanvas`'s `syncInvalidIndices` and outside the embedded-scene JSON, so the shared indices are never rewritten (AC E).
44	- The shared z-order actions (`zindex.ts`) are unchanged. My own Bring forward / Send backward still change the shared order and, on my screen, take effect within my layer (AC E).
45
46	### UI
47
48	In the collaborator dropdown, desktop and the phone main menu (same component):
49	- A **[Layering switch][Reset order]** row below Lock all / Unlock all. It reuses `Switch`. Reset order is disabled while layering is off and returns to the default order (me on top).
50	- While layering is on:
51	  - The rows become a single list in layer order, and #116's section titles become small per-row labels.
52	  - Each row, including mine and "Untagged & unknown", gets ↑, a drag handle, and ↓. They reuse the z-order and dots icons.
53	  - The top row's ↑ and the bottom row's ↓ are disabled.
54	  - Dragging the handle onto a row moves the dragged row there, using native drag and drop. A drop line shows where the row will land: above the target when dragging up, below it when dragging down. The whole list accepts the drag, so the cursor stays the same across rows and gaps. Dragging is off while filtering by name; the arrows still work.
55	- While layering is off, the dropdown renders exactly as in #116/#81.
```

```text
64	## Tech Debt
65
66	**Introduced:**
67
68	- The default order relies on `collaboratorDirectory` (a `Map`) keeping insertion order as the join order. `Map` guarantees this, but nothing in the code states it as a rule.
69	- The ordering runs in two cached places: the renderer's element map and App's `getElementsInDrawingOrder`. Both call the same function, so they can't disagree, but each sorts once per scene change.
70	- While layering is on, the dropdown renders its own list branch next to #116's sections branch. They share the `Row` component but not the list markup.
71	- `excalidraw-app/tests/collabLayer.test.tsx` duplicates about 60 lines of socket, encryption, and Firebase mocks from `collabLock.test.tsx`, because `vi.mock` applies per file (as in #81).
72	- Tests look actions up by name (`actionManager.actions[name]`), as #81's do, so a renamed action is caught at test time, not by the type checker.
```

## Commit 4: merging master

It brings in #178 (pages) and #84 (co-ownership). The one conflict was in `en.json`: both sides added a string group in the same spot, and both are kept. Nothing else needed hand-merging.

## Commit 5: co-owned elements in their highest visible owner's layer

**The rule, in `orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer`.** Each element is now ranked by all of its owners, using #84's `getElementVisibilityBuckets`, not just its creator. Hidden owners are skipped. If every owner is hidden, the highest owner is used; the element isn't drawn then anyway.

```ts
const getRank = (element: T) => {
  const buckets = getElementVisibilityBuckets(
    element,
    map,
    state.collaboratorDirectory,
  );
  const visibleBuckets = buckets.filter(
    (bucket) => !state.hiddenCollaboratorIds?.has(bucket),
  );
  return Math.max(
    ...(visibleBuckets.length ? visibleBuckets : buckets).map(
      (bucket) => rankByBucket.get(bucket) ?? -1,
    ),
  );
};
```

**Wiring.** The order now depends on who's hidden, so the renderer, App's cached drawing order and the SVG export pass `hiddenCollaboratorIds` into it. Each is a one- or two-line change.

**A one-line change to #84's code, which you should know about.** The new tests caught a real bug:

- **Before the fix:** after I edited Bob's shape and became its co-owner, clicking and export used the new layer, but the canvas still drew the shape in Bob's layer.
- **Cause:** #84 adds the co-owner without telling the scene anything changed. Its comment says it's "not a visual change for this client". With layering on it is, because the element can move up a layer, and our caches only refresh when the scene reports a change.
- **Fix:** in #84's listener in `App.tsx`, the scene is notified _only while layering is on_. With layering off, #84 behaves exactly as before, and all 16 of #84's co-ownership tests still pass.

**Tests: 13 new, each set with controls.**

- **7 unit tests** (`ownershipLayer.test.ts`), written first. 5 failed for the right reason, because the code still used the creator's layer only:
  - a single-owner control;
  - a co-owned element in its highest owner's layer;
  - the top owner hidden, so it's drawn in the highest visible owner's layer;
  - a hidden owner _below_ changes nothing;
  - every owner hidden;
  - a label on a co-owned shape;
  - a co-owner never seen, which counts as Miscellaneous.
- **6 editor tests** (`collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`). I become a co-owner through a real edit, as #84's tests do:
  - drawn in my higher layer;
  - clicking the overlap selects it. This test clicks once _before_ the edit, so it also catches stale caches;
  - hiding the higher co-owner (Bob) drops it to my layer, and showing Bob again moves it back;
  - the export uses the same order;
  - two controls showing what happens before the edit.
- With #84's line reverted, the drawing test fails, so the tests catch that bug.

**One slip, already fixed.** While checking the tests without the fix, my command to put the line back also changed an unrelated `informMutation: false` in the freehand-drawing code. I spotted it in the diff and put it back, and the final diff of `App.tsx` contains only the intended changes.

**`pr-82.md`** is updated with #84 in "Why" and "What changed", the co-owned rule, the change to #84's code, both new commits, two new tech-debt entries, a new Test Evidence row, the full test list (now 119), and your option-C decision in AI Usage. It's still uncommitted.

When you go over this, the parts to look at closely are the rank function above and the one-line change to #84's listener. After that the plan is unchanged: your Stryker run, then the coverage-gap pass, which now also includes switching pages while layering is on.

Here are the 13 new tests exactly as committed, each explained line by line with the reasoning behind its expected value, then what they cover and what they don't, then the updated flow.

## Part 1: the 7 unit tests (`ownershipLayer.test.ts`)

These call the ordering function directly, with no editor.

**Reading the arrays:** element lists are in drawing order, so the **last item is drawn on top**. Layer orders are written top row first.

### The new fixture

```ts
/** created by `creatorId`, co-owned (#84) by `editorIds` */
const createCoOwnedRect = (
  id: string,
  creatorId: string,
  editorIds: string[],
) => ({
  ...newElement({
    type: "rectangle",
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    customData: {
      [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId, // #116: who created it → "creatorId"
      [EDITOR_IDS_KEY]: editorIds, // #84: who co-owns it → "editorIds"
    },
  }),
  id, // readable id, set after construction (the type doesn't accept `id`)
});
```

This builds an element shaped exactly like #84 stores co-ownership: `customData.creatorId` plus `customData.editorIds`. I import #84's own key constant instead of typing `"editorIds"`, so a rename in #84 would break this test loudly rather than silently.

### The shared setup

```ts
describe("orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer — co-owned elements (#84, highest visible owner)", () => {
  const ALICE_TOP = ["alice", "me", "bob", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID];
  const myRect = createRect("my-rect", "me");
```

- `ALICE_TOP` is the layer order Alice → me → Bob → Miscellaneous. Ranked from the bottom: Bob is lowest, then me, then Alice on top.
- `myRect` is a plain single-owner shape of mine, sitting in the _middle_ layer. It's the yardstick: whether the test element ends up before or after `my-rect` shows which layer it landed in.
- The `layered(order, extra)` helper (from Phase 2) builds the state: me, Alice and Bob in the room and in the directory, layering on, and the given order plus any extra fields such as `hiddenCollaboratorIds`.

### Test 1: control

```ts
it("(control) without co-owners, an element is drawn in its creator's layer", () => {
  const bobOnly = createRect("bob-only", "bob"); // owned by Bob only
  expect(
    ids(
      orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer([bobOnly, myRect], layered(ALICE_TOP)),
    ),
  ).toEqual(["bob-only", "my-rect"]); // Bob (bottom) below me (middle)
});
```

- **Why:** without co-owners nothing new should happen. Bob's layer is below mine, so `bob-only` is drawn first and `my-rect` on top.
- **Role:** this is the baseline the next tests change. It passed before the change too, and it still passes after, which proves single-owner behavior didn't change.

### Test 2: co-owned → highest owner (AC B)

```ts
it("AC-B: a co-owned element is drawn in its highest owner's layer", () => {
  const shared = createCoOwnedRect("shared", "bob", ["alice"]); // created by Bob, co-owned by Alice
  expect(
    ids(orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer([shared, myRect], layered(ALICE_TOP))),
  ).toEqual(["my-rect", "shared"]); // now in Alice's (top) layer
});
```

- **Setup:** the same as the control, except the shape is co-owned by Alice.
- **Expected:** Alice is the top row, so option C ("highest visible owner") puts the shape in Alice's layer, above `my-rect`.
- **Before the change:** it was drawn in Bob's layer, giving `["shared", "my-rect"]`. It failed for exactly that reason.

### Test 3: highest owner hidden → next visible owner (AC G)

```ts
it("AC-G: with its highest owner hidden, it's drawn in its highest visible owner's layer", () => {
  const shared = createCoOwnedRect("shared", "bob", ["alice"]);
  expect(
    ids(
      orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer(
        [shared, myRect],
        layered(ALICE_TOP, { hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]) }), // Alice hidden
      ),
    ),
  ).toEqual(["shared", "my-rect"]); // falls to Bob's (bottom) layer
});
```

- **Why:** Alice is hidden. Under #84 the shape stays visible because Bob is visible, so it's drawn in the layer of the owner that keeps it visible: Bob's, below me.
- **What this checks:** "visible" really is part of the rule, so this is the test that tells option C apart from option B (B would keep it on top).
- **Before the change:** it already passed, because the old code used the creator (Bob) by coincidence.

### Test 4: hidden owner below changes nothing (AC G)

```ts
it("AC-G: a hidden owner below doesn't change its layer", () => {
  const shared = createCoOwnedRect("shared", "bob", ["alice"]);
  expect(
    ids(
      orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer(
        [shared, myRect],
        layered(ALICE_TOP, { hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["bob"]) }), // Bob (lower owner) hidden
      ),
    ),
  ).toEqual(["my-rect", "shared"]); // still Alice's layer
});
```

- **Why:** hiding the _lower_ owner must not move the shape, because the highest visible owner is still Alice.
- **What it guards against:** a filter that's backwards, for example keeping only hidden owners.
- **Before the change:** it failed (old code: Bob's layer).

### Test 5: every owner hidden

```ts
it("with every owner hidden, it keeps its highest owner's layer", () => {
  const shared = createCoOwnedRect("shared", "bob", ["alice"]);
  expect(
    ids(
      orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer(
        [shared, myRect],
        layered(ALICE_TOP, {
          hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice", "bob"]),
        }), // both hidden
      ),
    ),
  ).toEqual(["my-rect", "shared"]); // fallback: highest owner (Alice)
});
```

- **The case:** if every owner is hidden, the shape isn't drawn or clickable at all (#116/#84). It still needs a well-defined place in the order, because the function sorts the whole list.
- **The rule chosen:** fall back to the highest owner, so the element keeps the place it would have if it became visible again.
- **What it covers:** this is the only test that reaches the fallback branch.
- **Source of the expected value:** "Other". It's a design detail of the rule, not something the AC states.

### Test 6: a label follows its shape's owners (AC D)

```ts
it("AC-D: a label on a co-owned shape follows the shape's owners", () => {
  const container = createCoOwnedRect("container", "bob", ["alice"]); // shape: Bob + Alice
  const label = createLabel("label", "container", "me"); // label stamped by me
  expect(
    ids(
      orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer(
        [container, myRect, label],
        layered(ALICE_TOP),
      ),
    ),
  ).toEqual(["my-rect", "container", "label"]); // label right after its shape, in Alice's layer
});
```

- **Setup:** the label carries _my_ stamp, but its shape is owned by Bob and Alice. AC D says a label is always drawn with its container.
- **Expected:** shape and label move together to Alice's layer, with the label directly after the shape and `my-rect` below both. If the label followed its own stamp, it would stay in my layer and be split from its shape.
- **What it confirms:** #84's "a label follows its container's owners" works inside our sort.
- **Before the change:** it failed; the shape and label were both in Bob's layer.

### Test 7: an unseen co-owner counts as Miscellaneous (AC A)

```ts
it("AC-A: a co-owner this client never saw counts as the miscellaneous bucket", () => {
  const shared = createCoOwnedRect("shared", "bob", ["stranger"]); // "stranger" isn't in the directory
  expect(
    ids(
      orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer(
        [shared, myRect],
        layered([UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID, "alice", "me", "bob"]), // Miscellaneous on top
      ),
    ),
  ).toEqual(["my-rect", "shared"]); // shape goes to the Miscellaneous layer
});
```

- **Why:** #116 puts owners this client has never seen into the Miscellaneous bucket, and #84 does the same for co-owners. With Miscellaneous moved to the top, the shape's owners are Bob (bottom) and Miscellaneous (top), so it's drawn on top.
- **What it checks:** co-owners are mapped through the directory exactly like creators, and Miscellaneous is still an orderable row (AC A).
- **Before the change:** it failed.

## Part 2: the 6 editor tests (`collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`)

**Shared setup (unchanged).**

- The real editor, with `alice-under` and then `bob-over`, two filled squares at the same spot. Bob's square is on top in the shared order.
- Me, Alice and Bob are in the room. The default layer order is me → Alice → Bob.
- `drawnIds()` reads what App actually draws; `getSelectedIds()` reads the real selection.

### Helper 1: become a co-owner the real way

```ts
const coOwn = (id: string) => {
  API.setSelectedElements([getElement(id) as NonDeletedExcalidrawElement]); // 1. select Bob's shape
  execute("changeStrokeWidth", 4); // 2. a real edit, saved to undo history
  API.setSelectedElements([]); // 3. deselect, so later clicks aren't biased
  expect(getElement(id).customData?.[EDITOR_IDS_KEY]).toContain("me"); // 4. #84 really added me as co-owner
};
```

1. **Select Bob's shape.**
2. **Edit it with a real action.** This is the same edit #84's own tests use. #84 adds you as a co-owner only when a change you made directly is saved to undo history, so this goes through #84's real code path rather than writing the field by hand.
3. **Deselect.** The editor prefers the selected element when clicking, which would skew the click tests.
4. **Check #84 did its part.** If #84 ever stopped adding co-owners, the tests would fail here with a clear message, rather than later with a confusing ordering error.

### Helper 2: what the PNG export draws

```ts
const exportPngDrawOrder = async () => {
  const renderSpy = vi.spyOn(StaticScene, "renderStaticScene"); // watch the real renderer
  await exportToCanvas(
    h.elements.filter((el) => !el.isDeleted) as NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[],
    h.state, // full state: layering, order, hidden ids
    {},
    { exportBackground: false, viewBackgroundColor: "#ffffff" },
  );
  const drawn = renderSpy.mock.calls[0][0].visibleElements.map((el) => el.id); // the exact list it drew
  renderSpy.mockRestore();
  return drawn;
};
```

This is the same technique as the Phase 4 export tests: run the real PNG export and record the exact element list it hands to the renderer.

### Test 1: control, before co-owning

```ts
it("(control) before I edit Bob's shape, it's drawn in Bob's layer", () => {
  toggleLayering(); // default order: me, alice, bob
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["bob-over", "alice-under"]); // Bob is bottom → his shape is drawn first
});
```

**Why:** with the default order, Bob's layer is the lowest, so his square goes under Alice's even though it's on top in the shared order. This is the "before" picture for test 2.

### Test 2: after co-owning, drawn in my higher layer (AC B)

```ts
it("AC-B: after I edit Bob's shape I co-own it, so it's drawn in my higher layer", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  coOwn("bob-over"); // owners now: Bob + me
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["alice-under", "bob-over"]); // my layer (top) → above Alice
});
```

- **Expected:** the square's owners are now Bob (bottom) and me (top). Its highest visible owner is me, so it's drawn above Alice's square.
- **The bug it caught:** before the one-line change to #84's code, this test failed. #84 adds the co-owner without notifying the scene, so the canvas kept its stale cached order.
- **Shown to catch it:** with #84's line reverted, this is the test that fails.

### Test 3: control for clicking

```ts
it("AC-C: (control) before I edit Bob's shape, clicking the overlap selects Alice's shape on top", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  mouse.clickAt(50, 50); // real click on the overlap
  expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-under"]); // Alice is drawn on top, so she's clicked
});
```

**Why:** AC C says a click selects what's drawn on top, which before co-owning is Alice's square. This is the baseline for test 4.

### Test 4: after co-owning, the click follows (AC C), with a stale-cache check

```ts
it("AC-C: once I co-own Bob's shape, clicking the overlap selects it", () => {
  toggleLayering();
  // a click before co-owning, so the cached drawing order already exists
  mouse.clickAt(50, 50);
  expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["alice-under"]); // cache built with the OLD order
  coOwn("bob-over"); // order must now change…
  mouse.clickAt(50, 50);
  expect(getSelectedIds()).toEqual(["bob-over"]); // …and the click follows the new order
});
```

- **The first click** fills App's cached hit-test order on purpose, using the old order.
- **After co-owning,** the second click must select Bob's square, which is now drawn on top. That only works if the cache was refreshed.
- **Why it's written this way:** the earlier version of this test passed even with the bug, because nothing had built the cache yet. Now it checks the cache refresh too.

### Test 5: hide or show the higher co-owner (AC G)

```ts
it("AC-G: hiding its higher co-owner moves it to its highest visible owner's layer, and back when shown again", () => {
  API.setElements([...h.elements, stamp(createSolidRect("m1"), "me")]); // shared: alice-under, bob-over, m1
  toggleLayering();
  move("bob", 0); // order: bob, me, alice
  coOwn("bob-over"); // owners: Bob + me
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["alice-under", "m1", "bob-over"]); // highest visible owner = Bob (top)

  execute("toggleCollaboratorVisibility", "bob"); // hide Bob
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["alice-under", "bob-over", "m1"]); // now in MY layer; shared order puts it before m1

  execute("toggleCollaboratorVisibility", "bob"); // show Bob again
  expect(drawnIds()).toEqual(["alice-under", "m1", "bob-over"]); // back on top (AC G: drawn in place again)
});
```

- **Setup:** I add a shape of my own, `m1`, last in the shared order, and move Bob to the top row. After co-owning, `bob-over` belongs to Bob and me.
- **Bob visible:** the shape's highest visible owner is Bob, the top row, so it's drawn above everything, `m1` included.
- **Bob hidden:**
  - The shape stays visible because I'm still an owner (#84's rule).
  - Its highest visible owner is now me, so it drops into my layer.
  - Within my layer, `bob-over` comes before `m1` in the shared order, so it's drawn _under_ `m1` (AC B: shared order within a layer).
  - That one placement is what tells C apart from B: under B it would stay on top.
- **Bob shown again:** it returns to the top, matching AC G's "drawn in that place when shown again".
- **Also covered:** the renderer's cache refreshes when the hidden list changes.

### Test 6: export matches the canvas (AC I)

```ts
it("AC-I: the export draws a co-owned shape in the same layer as the canvas", async () => {
  toggleLayering();
  coOwn("bob-over");
  expect(await exportPngDrawOrder()).toEqual(["alice-under", "bob-over"]); // same as test 2's canvas order
});
```

**Why:** AC I says export follows my view. After co-owning, the PNG export draws the shapes in the same order as the canvas in test 2.

## Part 3: what the new tests cover

**The rank function, by branch.** Measured on the 7 unit tests alone:

| Branch in `getRank` | Hits | Covered by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hidden list present vs. absent (`hiddenCollaboratorIds?.has`) | 22 / 9 | Tests 3–5 (present); 1, 2, 6, 7 (absent) |
| At least one visible owner vs. all hidden (the `? :` fallback) | 14 / 1 | Every test / test 5 only |
| Owner found in the order vs. not (`?? -1`) | 20 / **0** | The "not found" branch is reached by the older AC H test, "creator missing from the order". So all 40 unit tests together cover every branch. |

**Wiring.**

- **Renderer passes the hidden list:** editor tests 2 and 5 (5 changes the hidden list while layering is on).
- **App's cached hit-test order:** editor test 4, including the refresh after co-owning.
- **#84's listener, layering on:** editor tests 2 and 4. Layering off: #84's own 16 tests, which all still pass.
- **PNG export:** editor test 6.

**What's still not covered:**

- **SVG export with a co-owned element and a hidden owner.** The `hiddenCollaboratorIds` line in `data/index.ts` _runs_ in the existing SVG export tests, but no test checks that hiding a co-owner changes the SVG order.
- **A click after hiding a co-owner.** Test 5 checks drawing, not clicking. The hit-test cache now uses the hidden list as part of its key, but no test clicks after hiding.
- **Binding to a co-owned shape.** It goes through the same function, but no test draws an arrow onto one.
- **Two co-owners besides me.** I can't act as two other clients in one editor test. The unit tests cover it with data built by hand.

These four join the list for the post-Stryker coverage pass, along with the earlier gaps and the page-switch case.

## Part 4: the updated flow

New or changed parts are marked **◆**.

```

                                       + #116 hiddenCollaboratorIds, collaboratorDirectory
                                       + #81  lockedCollaboratorIds

 Element data (shared, synced):  customData.creatorId (#116)  +  ◆ customData.editorIds / editorSeqs (#84)
          ▲

          │      adds me as co-owner (App's store listener)
          │      ◆ informMutation = collaboratorLayeringEnabled  → scene nonce bumps → caches refresh
          │
 ┌──────── element/src/ownership.ts ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ #84  getElementVisibilityBuckets(el) = [creator, ...co-owners] mapped through the directory      │
 │      (label → its container's owners; never-seen → Miscellaneous)                               │
 │ #84  isElementByHiddenCreator: hidden only if EVERY bucket is hidden                             │
 │ #84  isElementInteractive:     interactive if ANY bucket is interactive                          │
 │ #82  orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer:                                                           │
 │        off → same array                                                                          │
 │        on  → rank(el) = ◆ max layer rank over the el's VISIBLE buckets                           │

 │              stable sort by rank (shared order kept within a rank)                               │
 └────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬─────────────────┘
      ▼                      ▼                          ▼                       ▼
 Renderer               App.getElementsInDrawingOrder  binding.ts / focus.ts   export
 memo key: nonce,       memo key: nonce, layer order,  (appState includes      prepareElementsForRender
 layer order, hidden,   directory, ◆ hidden ids         hidden ids already)     PNG: full appState
 directory              → hit-test → #84 interactive                            ◆ SVG: + hiddenCollaboratorIds
 ◆ passes hidden ids      filter (any owner) → click                            (via exportCanvas)
```

**Walking through it, with Bob's shape that I edit:**

1. **The edit is saved.** I change Bob's shape. When the change is saved to undo history, #84's listener adds me to `editorIds`.
2. **The scene is notified (the change to #84's code).** With layering on, the listener now tells the scene. Its version counter moves on, so the renderer's and App's cached orders are rebuilt.
3. **The new rank.** The ordering function reads the shape's owners via #84's `getElementVisibilityBuckets` (Bob and me), drops any that are hidden, and ranks the shape by the highest remaining layer.
4. **Everything else follows.** Rendering, clicking, binding and export all call that function, so they agree on the shape's new place. Clicks then go through #84's interactivity rule: it's clickable if any owner is unlocked.
5. **Hiding an owner.** `hiddenCollaboratorIds` changes. It's part of the renderer's and App's cache keys, so the shape is redrawn in its next visible owner's layer without any scene change.
6. **What's still untouched:** shared indices, z-order, sync and undo history. The co-owner stamp is #84's existing, already-synced data; layering adds nothing to what's sent.

Read #84's co-ownership rule

```text
// co-ownership: editing someone else's element makes you a co-owner
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Element properties whose change doesn't count as editing the element:
 * bookkeeping, z-order, and references updated as a side effect of editing
 * other elements (e.g. binding an arrow updates the shape's `boundElements`).
 */
const NON_EDIT_PROPS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "version",
  "versionNonce",
  "updated",
  "seed",
  "index",
  "boundElements",
  "customData",
]);

const isSameValue = (a: unknown, b: unknown) =>
  a === b ||
  (typeof a === "object" &&
    typeof b === "object" &&
    a !== null &&
    b !== null &&
    JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b));

/** whether going from `prev` to `next` edits the element (see NON_EDIT_PROPS) */
export const isOwnershipEdit = (
  prev: ExcalidrawElement,
  next: ExcalidrawElement,
): boolean => {
  for (const key of new Set([...Object.keys(prev), ...Object.keys(next)])) {
    if (
      !NON_EDIT_PROPS.has(key) &&
      !isSameValue(
        prev[key as keyof ExcalidrawElement],
        next[key as keyof ExcalidrawElement],
      )
    ) {
      return true;
    }
  }
  return false;
};

/** structurally satisfied by the editor's AppState */
export type CoOwnershipEditState = CreatorSelf & {
  selectedElementIds: Readonly<Record<string, true>>;
  editingTextElement?: Readonly<{ id: string }> | null;
  selectedLinearElement?: Readonly<{ elementId: string }> | null;
};

/**
 * Whether the user acted on the element directly: it (or the shape a label
 * belongs to) is selected, being text-edited, or having its points edited.
 * Elements changed as a side effect (an arrow rerouted because the shape it's
 * bound to moved, a dragged frame's children…) don't count.
 */
const isDirectlyEdited = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  holder: ExcalidrawElement,
  state: CoOwnershipEditState,
): boolean =>
  !!state.selectedElementIds[element.id] ||
  !!state.selectedElementIds[holder.id] ||
  state.editingTextElement?.id === element.id ||
  state.selectedLinearElement?.elementId === element.id;

/** whether `clientId` is the element's creator or one of its co-owners */
export const isElementOwnedBy = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  clientId: string,
): boolean =>
  getStampedCreatorId(element) === clientId ||
  getStampedEditorIds(element).includes(clientId);

/**
 * Elements this client edited without owning them, so it becomes a co-owner.
 * Compares the scene against the last committed snapshot, so it's meant to
 * run right before a change is captured into history (the stamp then lands in
 * the same undo entry as the edit, and undoing that edit removes it).
 *
 * Returns the elements holding the ownership (bound text → its container),
 * de-duplicated. Only elements that already existed and carry a creator stamp
 * qualify: new elements get the creator stamp, not a co-owner stamp.
 */
export const getElementsToCoOwn = (
  prevElements: ElementsMap,
  nextElements: ElementsMap,
  state: CoOwnershipEditState,
  selfId: string | null = getSelfCreatorId(state),
): ExcalidrawElement[] => {
  if (!selfId) {
    return [];
  }

  const toCoOwn = new Map<string, ExcalidrawElement>();
  for (const next of nextElements.values()) {
    const prev = prevElements.get(next.id);
    if (!prev || prev.version >= next.version || next.isDeleted) {
      continue;
    }
    const holder = getOwnershipHolder(next, nextElements);
    if (
      holder.isDeleted ||
      toCoOwn.has(holder.id) ||
      !getStampedCreatorId(holder) ||
      isElementOwnedBy(holder, selfId) ||
      !isDirectlyEdited(next, holder, state) ||
      !isOwnershipEdit(prev, next)
    ) {
      continue;
    }
    toCoOwn.set(holder.id, holder);
  }
  return [...toCoOwn.values()];
};

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// the co-owner set: one entry per client, changed only by that client
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

</details></tool-use>

## What makes an element owned by both

It's #84's rule (`getElementsToCoOwn` in `ownership.ts`). #82 only reads the result. **You become a co-owner of someone else's element when all of these are true:**

1. **The change is saved to undo history.** The check runs just before an edit becomes an undo step. Our layering actions are never undo steps, so they can't create co-ownership.
2. **You acted on it directly.** The element, or the shape a label belongs to, is selected, being text-edited, or having its points edited. Side effects don't count: an arrow rerouted because its shape moved, or a frame's children moving with the frame.
3. **It's a real edit,** meaning some property other than bookkeeping changed. Changes to `version`, `updated`, `index` (z-order), `boundElements` and `customData` don't count. So moving, resizing or restyling Bob's shape co-owns it; Bring forward on it doesn't.
4. **It isn't already yours, and it existed before.** New elements get a creator stamp instead, and you're never added twice.
5. **You're in a room.** Outside one there's no client id to stamp.

**What gets stored:**

- Your id is added to `customData.editorIds`, next to #116's `creatorId`.
- A counter for you in `customData.editorSeqs` goes up. It lets clients merge co-owner lists when copies disagree: the higher counter is the newer state.
- Editing a label co-owns its shape.

**Undo:** undoing _all_ your edits to the element removes you again, and redo adds you back. Your removal leaves a marker so an older copy can't bring you back.

**Limits that follow from these rules:**

- You can't co-own a hidden or locked element, because you can't select or edit it.
- Co-ownership arriving from other clients syncs like any other change. It reaches the canvas through a normal scene update, so the stale-cache fix I made was only needed for your _own_ edits.

## How this affects future work

**Elements now change layers by themselves.** Before #84, an element's layer only changed when _you_ reordered rows. Now it also moves:

- when anyone edits it, on any client;
- when an owner is hidden or shown;
- when an edit is undone.

Expected effects:

- **Edits look like a jump.** I expect a shape you drag to stay in its creator's layer until you release it, then jump to yours, because the co-owner is added when the edit is saved. I haven't checked this in the browser, so it's worth looking at in your manual test.
- **Diagrams can split across layers.** If Alice restyles one box of Bob's diagram, that box draws in Alice's layer and the rest stays in Bob's, so a diagram or group can end up interleaved with other people's work. #84 itself works per element, and its PR notes it has no group test. Ranking a group by its highest-ranked member would fix this. I'd log it as tech debt or a follow-up issue rather than expand #82.
- **You can't fully bury someone's work.** A collaborator's element that someone higher has co-edited stays high. That's the "least restricted owner" choice working as intended, but it's worth saying in the PR so reviewers aren't surprised.

**The two features are now linked in code.** #84's listener in `App.tsx` checks #82's layering switch. Two rules for anyone changing these features later:

- Anything new that affects layer order (per-element priority, page-specific orders, group ranking) must be added to the cache keys in `Renderer.ts` and App's `getLayeredElements`, or must notify the scene, as #84's listener now does. Otherwise you get the same stale-canvas bug the tests caught today.
- If #84 ever stops notifying the scene, or batches its stamps, editor test 2 ("after I edit Bob's shape… drawn in my higher layer") will fail. That's intended: it protects the link.

**The single ordering function is the place to extend.** Everything (canvas, clicks, binding, export) reads one rank per element. Future changes slot into `getRank`:

- per-element priority (out of scope for #82);
- group-level ranking;
- default orders for new users (#83 builds on `getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder`);
- a different co-ownership policy.

Changing the rule in one place changes everywhere at once.

**Data and performance.**

- **Per-element cost.** With layering on, the rank is computed per element whenever the scene or the order changes: one entry per owner, then a sort. That's fine at today's sizes.
- **Lists only grow.** #84 never cleans up its removal markers, and owner lists don't shrink, so long-lived rooms make each element's owner list longer. Cleaning that up belongs to #84, but it would slightly reduce our sort's work too.

**Tests.**

- The unit tests write `editorIds` as an array, using #84's own key constant. If #84 changes how co-owners are stored, those fixtures need updating.
- The editor tests go through #84's real edit flow, so they'll keep matching whatever #84 does.

**PR notes.** I'd add two lines to `pr-82.md`:

- Tech debt, Introduced: a co-edited element jumps layers when the edit is saved, and a co-edited diagram can split across layers.
- Not tested: group or diagram behavior under co-ownership.

Do you want those added?

```text
9-What is one thing you learned about testing in your project?
10-
11-I learned that changing a data model means testing old data as well as the new feature. Replacing the old filter: "grayscale" field with a filter stack could have broken drawings people had already saved. So I wrote tests that load scenes in the old format and check that they migrate correctly, and that bad values fall back to safe defaults. I also learned that one feature can have several renderers: the canvas, SVG export and a Safari fallback. Putting all the filter ranges and clamping in one shared module meant I could test the logic once and trust all three to agree. Excalidraw's snapshot tests also caught UI changes I hadn't meant to make.
```

```text
15:A user is reviewing a teammate's diagram in a busy room, but other collaborators have drawn large shapes on top of it. They open the collaborator dropdown, grab the handle next to the teammate's name, and drag them to the top of the list. The teammate's diagram is now drawn above everyone else's on their screen, and clicking where the drawings overlap selects the teammate's element they can see. They press the down arrow on another collaborator to move them one place lower. Later they press **Reset order** and the original shared order returns. Nobody else in the room sees any change.
27:**Reason:** Builds on #116 and #81: ownership (`customData.creatorId`), the per-collaborator dropdown, and local-only AppState are already in place. This issue adds a local layer order and a single pure ordering function, and applies it everywhere drawing order matters: canvas rendering, hit-testing (so the element you click is the one you see on top), and export. It also adds a reorderable list to the dropdown, with drag-and-drop plus up/down arrow buttons. The drag-and-drop UI and the renderer/hit-test changes make this larger than #81, but it needs no new ownership, sync, or server work.
```
